Acknowledgement of Country

The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority proudly acknowledges and pays respect to Victoria’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and their rich and enduring cultures.

We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as Australia’s first peoples and as the Traditional Owners and custodians of the lands and waters on which we rely. We pay respect to Elders past and present of the lands where we conduct our work and recognise their ongoing contributions as the first educators on the land now known as Victoria.

Watch now: To find out more about this curriculum area, watch ‘Understanding the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0, Indonesian’ on the Resources page.

Rationale and Aims

Rationale

Communication is a human imperative. Communication in Indonesian involves interaction to convey meaning, as well as imagination, creativity and a broad understanding of ourselves and others. Language learning provides the opportunity for students to engage with the linguistic and cultural diversity of the world and its peoples, and to reflect on their experience in various aspects of social life, including their own participation and ways of being in the world. 

Learning Indonesian broadens students’ horizons in relation to the personal, social, cultural and employment opportunities that an increasingly interconnected and interdependent world can offer. The interdependence of countries and communities means people in all spheres of life are required to negotiate experiences and meanings across languages and cultures. A capability solely in English, despite its status as a world language, can limit global opportunities. A bilingual or plurilingual capability is the norm in many parts of the world. 

Learning Indonesian develops learners’: 

  • communication skills 
  • literacy skills in their first and additional languages 
  • intercultural capabilities 
  • understanding of, and respect for, diversity and difference, and openness to different experiences and perspectives 
  • understanding and appreciation of how culture shapes worldviews, and extends their understanding of themselves, and their own heritage, values, culture and identity 
  • critical and creative thinking. 

Indonesian has been the official and national language of Indonesia since the country’s independence. It is a language used throughout the Indonesian archipelago, which comprises over 17,000 islands. It is closely related to Malay and other variants used in Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and southern Thailand. 

Contact has taken place between Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples of northern Australia and the peoples of the islands now known as Indonesia for several centuries, with the sharing of art, commerce, cuisine, culture and language. Indonesia is Australia’s largest neighbour in the South-East Asian region of the Asia-Pacific and therefore commercial, cultural and linguistic ties continue to be of great significance between the 2 countries.  

Indonesian has been taught in some Australian schools and universities since the 1950s. Relations between Indonesia and Australia continue to grow in the area of education as well as trade and cultural exchanges. Australia has a strong diplomatic presence in Indonesia and significant numbers of Australians travel to Indonesia for education, business and leisure. There is an increasing number of Indonesian-speaking communities across Australia.  

Learning Indonesian enhances students’ understanding of their own language(s) and develops their appreciation of the language and cultures of Indonesian-speaking communities. It also enriches travel experiences, increases employment opportunities, and promotes understanding of diverse attitudes, beliefs and values. 

Learning Indonesian provides opportunities for students to engage socially, culturally and economically in many domains, such as business, trade, science, law, education, tourism, diplomacy, international relations, health and communications.  

Aims 

The 4 interrelated aims of the Indonesian language curriculum are to develop knowledge, understanding and skills to ensure students: 

  • communicate in Indonesian 
  • understand the relationship between language and culture 
  • develop intercultural capabilities 
  • understand themselves as communicators.

Structure

Pathways 

Indonesian has been developed as a Second Language Learner Pathway, which caters for students learning Indonesian as a second or additional language.  

Sequences 

Indonesian is presented in 2 sequences that offer different entry points into language learning: 

  • F–10 Sequence, for students who begin to learn the language in Prep and continue to Year 10
  • 7–10 Sequence, for students who begin to learn the language in Year 7 and continue to Year 10. 

The VCAA acknowledges that these 2 sequences do not necessarily represent the variety of entry points into the curriculum. Teachers can use the sequences flexibly to meet the needs of their students by making appropriate adjustments to differentiate learning experiences and cater for learners of different backgrounds. 

The F–10 Sequence is presented in 5 curriculum bands, beginning with Foundation to Level 2, followed by Levels 3 and 4, Levels 5 and 6, Levels 7 and 8, and Levels 9 and 10. The 7–10 Sequence is presented in 2 bands: Levels 7 and 8, and Levels 9 and 10.  

Strands and sub-strands 

Content in Indonesian is organised under 3 interrelated strands, each with a number of sub-strands (as shown in Table 1). 

Table 1: Strands and sub-strands within the Indonesian curriculum

Engaging with Indonesian Language and Culture 

This entry-level strand appears in Foundation to Level 2 only. It involves students’ early exploration of and play with language learning. There are 2 sub-strands. 

Engaging with Indonesian language 

Developing receptive language skills in the classroom environment; exploring, noticing, listening and recognising, and then progressing to responding and using oral communication.  

Engaging with Indonesian culture 

Exploring and noticing connections between language and culture. 

Communicating Meaning in Indonesian 

This strand involves students learning to use language for communicative purposes in interpreting, creating and exchanging meaning. There are 3 sub-strands.  

Interacting in Indonesian 

Communicating and exchanging ideas, opinions, experiences, thoughts and feelings in non-verbal, spoken and written interactions; participating in planning, negotiating, deciding and taking action. 

Mediating meaning in and between languages  

Locating, obtaining, interpreting and conveying information through a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts; moving between languages and cultures non-verbally, orally and in writing; recognising different interpretations. 

Creating text in Indonesian 

Creating a range of spoken and written texts for specific contexts, purposes and audiences. 

Understanding Language and Culture  

This strand involves students learning to analyse and understand language and culture as resources for interpreting and shaping meaning in intercultural exchange. There are 2 sub-strands. 

Understanding systems of language  

Understanding the linguistic features of the language, including sound, writing, and grammatical and textual conventions. 

Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture  

Analysing and reflecting on the role of language and culture in shaping meaning and identity. 

Achievement standards 

Achievement standards describe what students are typically able to understand and do, and they are the basis for reporting student achievement. 

In Indonesian, students progress along a learning continuum. The learning sequence undertaken by students will determine the number and progression of achievement standards: 

  • F–10 Sequence – the first achievement standard is provided at Level 2 and then at Levels 4, 6, 8 and 10
  • 7–10 Sequence – the first achievement standard is provided at Level 8 and then at Level 10. 

Content descriptions 

In Indonesian, content descriptions sequence and describe the knowledge, understanding and skills that teachers need to teach and students are expected to learn. 

Elaborations 

Elaborations are examples that provide guidance on how the curriculum may be transformed into a classroom activity or learning opportunity. They are provided as advisory material only.

Learning in Indonesian

Indonesian is pitched to second and additional language learners, who are the dominant group of Indonesian language learners in the current Australian context.  

Students of Indonesian in Victorian schools come from a range of backgrounds. Most students will be learning Indonesian for the first time, while some may have existing connections to Indonesian through early learning experiences or as background Indonesian speakers. 

Indonesian language 

The Indonesian language uses a Romanised script and has phonetic pronunciation, so speakers of English can predict how to say, read or write Indonesian words. It has several sounds that require learning, such as the trilled r, the ‘ch’ sound of the letter c, the combined vowel sounds ai and au, the distinction between ng and ngg, and the glottal stop k when it is a final syllable.  

Indonesian grammar is characterised by a system of affixation, where prefixes and suffixes attached to base words form new words belonging to different word classes or with changed grammatical function. The most common among these that are relevant to this curriculum are the noun and verb forms using the prefixes ber-, me-, pe- and ke-, and the suffixes -kan, -i and -an. 

There is a significant distinction between oral and written, as well as formal and informal, Indonesian. Written language, for example, follows grammatical rules of affixation, whereas spoken language often drops affixes, and vowels are often reduced to single sounds; for example, the formal hijau often appears informally as ijo. Spoken language is also frequently combined with local languages and slang forms. 

A major feature of Indonesian is its extensive pronoun system, which can be quite simple in its initial stages (for example, saya, Anda, kamu) but becomes increasingly complex, with multiple forms according to situations and contexts of use. In addition, the use of object-focus construction is marked, and it is frequently used in both spoken and written contexts to create distance between the agent and the action. 

Macro skills  

The macro skills of listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing – also known as language modes – are interrelated. The learning of one skill often supports and extends the learning of others. To acknowledge these interrelationships, content in the Languages curriculums incorporates these macro skills in an integrated and interdependent way. 

Teaching and learning contexts will necessarily draw from more than one of these skills to support students’ effective learning. For example, students will learn new vocabulary, such as words, phrases and expressions, through listening, reading and viewing. They will apply their knowledge and understanding in their speaking and writing, as well as in their comprehension of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts.  

The macro skills are strongly aligned to all 3 strands in the Indonesian curriculum (as shown in Table 2) and are implicit in the content of the sub-strands and across the content descriptions.

Texts 

Students use a wide range of texts designed for language learning, such as textbooks, teacher-generated materials and online resources. Learning is enriched by exposure to a range of authentic Indonesian texts, such as websites, films, stories, songs, television programs, advertisements and magazines.  

Texts can be spoken, written, viewed or multimodal, and in print or digital/online forms. They include all forms of augmentative and alternative communication; for example, gestures, real objects, photographs and images. Multimodal texts combine different modes of communication such as images and written or spoken language.  

Texts provide important opportunities for learning about languages and cultures. Purposeful activities can be organised around texts to meet the needs of the students in the classroom. Many of the tasks that students undertake in and out of school involve understanding and producing texts in everyday and workplace contexts. 

Teachers are best placed to guide the selection of texts for students to listen to, read, view, write and create. The texts and resources will become increasingly sophisticated and varied as students progress through their schooling.  

Teachers in government schools should refer to the Department of Education social media use policy if using social media texts, such as blogs, with students. Teachers in Catholic and independent schools should refer to their sector authorities for advice on social media policies.  

Intercultural understanding 

In the Languages curriculum area, the focus is on both language and culture, as students learn to communicate meaningfully across linguistic and cultural systems, and different contexts. This process involves reflection and analysis, as students move between Indonesian, English and/or their own existing language(s). It is a reciprocal and dynamic process that develops language use and intercultural awareness and understanding. 

The use of Indonesian and English 

Students should use Indonesian to communicate whenever possible in classroom, local or digital environments. The use of English provides opportunities for students to reflect on, explore and discuss ideas, and to use metalanguage to talk about and compare languages and cultures.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Indonesian Foundation to Level 2 (Curriculum F–10 Sequence)

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Foundation to Level 2, Indonesian language learning builds on the Victorian Early Years Learning and Development Framework and each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. In the early stages, the focus is on engagement through imagination and play-based learning. Students first engage with the language and culture through listening, speaking and action-related learning activities. They participate in shared listening and viewing of multimodal texts that reflect the language and cultures of Indonesian-speaking communities. 

Students learn to communicate with others, and a focus on play is a strong feature throughout this band. They imitate the sounds, shapes and patterns of spoken Indonesian, and receive extensive support through modelling, scaffolding and revisiting their learning as their understanding develops. Learners explore the written language, beginning with reading a variety of texts and progressing to creating their own texts about their personal world as they develop their linguistic skills. 

Through engaging with texts of increasing depth and complexity, students are given opportunities to expand their linguistic repertoire. They develop their vocabulary and identify and explain their understanding of language and grammatical features using simple metalanguage. 

Culture and language are intertwined throughout every facet of language learning, and students discover that what is familiar to one person can be new to another.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 2, students identify the different sounds and rhythms of the Indonesian language by listening to and viewing a variety of texts. They compare these sounds with other languages, noticing how pronunciation changes and discovering how languages are influenced by each other. They explore Indonesian through play, first imitating sounds and patterns, then replicating expressions and phrases, before producing responses using formulaic and familiar language. They recognise that Indonesian sounds are represented by letters, and they can match these with words, combining them in increasingly complex ways. They develop and expand their vocabulary, from simple sounds to frequently used words and phrases, using the pronunciation and intonation patterns of spoken Indonesian. They expand their repertoire of Indonesian words and phrases through listening and reading, then progress to creating simple sentences and responses using modelled language.

Students identify familiar words and phrases to obtain meaning from a variety of multimodal texts relating to their personal world. They begin to explain their understanding of the features and grammatical structures of Indonesian using simple metalanguage. They start to develop written competence by copying letters and words, and then produce the language with support. They respond to texts using frequently used words, phrases and sentence patterns in both written and spoken language. They apply their understanding of some of the conventions and features of the written Indonesian language. They use common grammatical structures to create their own simple texts, with the support of visual and/or spoken cues.

Students explore and recognise the influence of culture on language and identity. They recognise that Indonesian is spoken in communities and regions in Australia and around the world, and relate this to their own language(s) and culture(s)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring similarities and differences in onomatopoeia in Indonesian and other languages represented in the classroom, for example, gong-gong (woof, woof), meong (miaow), kwek-kwek (quack, quack), cit-cit (tweet, tweet), hacciihh (achoo) and kring-kring (ding, ding)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: explore and make meaning from sounds, words and phrases for familiar objects or terms in Indonesian through play, and discover how languages influence each other
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a range of games (e.g. matching pairs, filling in gaps, drag-and-drop, memory games, bingo), using secure digital tools and applications to reinforce vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping vocabulary (e.g. classroom objects, animals) into sets by using word cards and/or images, and playing games (e.g. buzz, around the world) to practise numbers or other vocabulary sets

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: following numerical notation to perform a collaborative musical piece on the angklung

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a treasure hunt finding objects related to colour, number, classroom items, for example, tiga buku merah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using familial terms of address in wider contexts, for example, Ibu/Bapak for teachers and adults

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages have loan words and that many Indonesian words are used in English (e.g. bamboo, orangutan, gecko, papaya) by creating a categories chart to list words from different languages, or playing a sorting game to sort words into their language of origin

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that many English words are used in Indonesian and may include variations in spelling (e.g. foto; akses; buku; kartun; dokter)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK2
organising_ideas.text: The interrelationships between people and the diverse environments and systems across the Asia region have global implications.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing physical or digital board games (e.g. 4 in a row, concentration, snakes and ladders, bingo) that have been modified to help students learn vocabulary or practise question-and-answer exchanges

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing role-plays such as buying fruits and vegetables, or acting as a character from a story that is familiar to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster to explain greetings at different times of the day (e.g. Selamat pagi; Selamat siang; Selamat sore; Selamat malam) and discussing the meaning of the word selamat

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2U01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: imitate the pronunciation and intonation of spoken Indonesian, and understand how sounds are produced

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting the Indonesian alphabet and/or singing alphabet rhymes/songs, and noticing that the Indonesian and English alphabets are both based on the Roman alphabet, but that the letters have different names in Indonesian and represent different sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: repeating words and phrases to imitate authentic Indonesian pronunciation, intonation and rhythm

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating Indonesian pronunciation, for example, vowels, trilled r, c (‘ch’) and the unaspirated sounds p, t and k especially at the end of a word (e.g. empat, nenek)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian has pure vowel sounds and each vowel sound is represented by one letter

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the vowel e has 3 different pronunciations: enam, sate, enak

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising diphthongs, for example, au in mau and ai in main

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: clapping the rhythm of syllables to notice even word stress

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that statements, commands and questions have different intonations

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2U04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken Indonesian has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing similarities in raising intonation at the end of questions and understanding the difference between statements, questions and exclamations

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing noun+adjective word order differences, for example, kucing hitam; mobil merah; bis besar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing difference in spontaneous exclamations in Indonesian and English, for example, Wah!; Aduh!, and sharing other examples from languages represented within the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian sentences use a subject+verb+object structure; noticing that this is similar to English sentences; and discussing similarities and differences with other known languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English represent cardinal numbers in the same way

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian forms plurals in different ways from English such as by duplicating, using a number or a qualifier, for example, kursi-kursi, dua kursi, banyak kursi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English divide the day differently, for example, comparing ‘good morning’ and ‘good afternoon’ with Selamat pagi and Selamat siang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in Indonesian siblings are identified in relation to position in the family, for example, kakak (older sibling), and discussing any other known languages that may identify family members in the same way

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that features of familiar texts may be similar or different in Indonesian and English, for example, the chorus of a song; the lines of a nursery rhyme or poem

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has some loan words from English (e.g. komputer, televisi), and that English has some from Indonesian (e.g. orangutan, satay, rambutan) with some changes in spelling, then noticing that some Australian English terms or expressions have no equivalent in Indonesian (e.g. koala, meat pie, farm), and that this is also the case with some Indonesian terms or expressions (e.g. becak, Kancil, mudik)

as_extracts.name: LINDF102-E03
as_extracts.description: They explore Indonesian through play, first imitating sounds and patterns, then replicating expressions and phrases, before producing responses using formulaic and familiar language.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2E02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: develop oral language skills through exploring and listening to the sounds and patterns of the language
content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Indonesian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting the teacher in Indonesian, when their name is called on the roll or through choral class greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in songs and chants, for example, ‘Topi Saya Bundar’, ‘Lingkaran Kecil Lingkaran Besar’ and ‘Satu Satu Aku Sayang Ibu’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous Indonesian exclamations when interacting with peers, for example, Aduh!; Wah!; Bagus!; Hebat!; Hati-hati!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: clapping the number of syllables in common words as they say them, for example, clapping the syllables in greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing bingo with images, sounds, words or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising short tongue twisters or rhymes

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring sounds with onomatopoeia, for example, learning the sounds of different animals

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with new sets of vocabulary by making concrete associations with them, such as touching and identifying colours in the classroom, or touching and identifying soft-toy animals and naming them

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2E03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: recognise and respond to greetings, instructions and language relating to their personal world using one- or 2-word responses and/or single-idea phrases
content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Indonesian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting teacher and peers, for example, Selamat pagi, Bu/Pak; Selamat siang, Ari

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to routine questions, for example, Apa kabar?; Siapa nama kamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to classroom instructions, for example, Duduk; Berdiri; Diam; Ambil lem; Tutup pintu, with appropriate actions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming a circle and creating a question-and-answer routine, asking the student next to them and so forth, for example, Namaku Alya. Siapa namamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to games or songs with actions, for example, ‘Kepala, Pundak, Lutut, Kaki’

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2E04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Indonesian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing suit/suten/suwitan or hompimpa to decide who goes first in games

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing and engaging with cultural items from Indonesia, such as coins, postcards and authentic items

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: play-acting with dress-ups and props or with puppets when participating in role-plays

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected to various languages, cultures and traditions according to specific ethnic groups and regions in Indonesia, for example, in Javanese culture eating nasi tumpeng on celebratory occasions like birthdays or ketupat during Eid

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning Indonesian terms through the arts and culture, for example, topeng when making masks, batik when making modified batik art, wayang when playing with leather puppets

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring similarities and differences in onomatopoeia in Indonesian and other languages represented in the classroom, for example, gong-gong (woof, woof), meong (miaow), kwek-kwek (quack, quack), cit-cit (tweet, tweet), hacciihh (achoo) and kring-kring (ding, ding)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting classmates and teacher, for example, Selamat pagi, Apa kabar? Baik, terima kasih.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for permission, for example, Boleh saya ke kamar kecil?, Boleh saya pinjam pensilmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using everyday Indonesian formulaic expressions, for example, Maaf; Permisi; Terima kasih; Silakan; Sama-sama; Ayo

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class, introducing themselves and responding to everyday personal questions such as Berapa umurmu? Di mana kamu tinggal? Apakah Anda punya hewan peliharaan?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming family members and friends and noticing the difference between the formal and informal forms, such as Ibu/Bu; Bapak/Pak; Nenek/Nek; Kakek/Kek; Adik/Dek

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and sharing simple expressions and songs with friends and family, for example, singing ‘Selamat ulang tahun’ and using appropriate greetings (e.g. Halo!; Selamat pagi / siang / sore / malam!) for different times or occasions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or printouts from popular shows or cartoons to role-play greetings and exchange information, imagining themselves as the character

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using PowerPoint slides or image flashcards to show different pictures (using taught vocabulary) to elicit responses

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple descriptive or expressive statements to describe themselves and to express their likes, preferences or feelings (e.g. Saya berusia lima tahun; Saya orang Australia; Saya suka olahraga; Saya lebih suka menari; Saya senang sekali), for example, creating a flipbook (on paper or digitally), drawing/pasting in images to support their sentences

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: generating phrases (e.g. Saya sedih; Saya sakit) using props such as images of faces with different expressions, for example, randomly distributing emoji faces attached to an icy pole stick and asking each student, Bagaimana keadaanmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to questions such as Apa ini/itu?, Ada berapa …?, Apa warna pensil ini? and Siapa ini?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing preferences such as choosing objects, for example, Saya mau … / Saya tidak mau … / Saya suka … / Saya kurang suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared performance of songs and chants with appropriate gestures, for example, ‘Kepala, Pundak, Lutut, Kaki’; Selamat Pagi, Pak. Selamat Pagi, Bu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-plays using modelled expressions and appropriate gestures in known scenarios such as introductions or shopping at a market, for example, Mau beli apa? Satu nanas dan dua pisang; Berapa harganya? Wah, mahal!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing number games (e.g. buzz and bingo), and using Indonesian to count places in dice games such as snakes and ladders

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing guessing games such as hot and cold or celebrity heads

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using mime and actions to demonstrate understanding, for example, miming a cat pose in response to the word kucing, responding to instructions such as duduk or berdiri with appropriate action, engaging in movement games such as jumping to a coloured spot, forming groups corresponding to teacher commands such as merah, tiga

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information in a spoken or written text to label, or draw a picture, for example, dia bermata biru

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images in catalogues, naming toys and games such as Kelereng Gundu, and selecting and listing items and prices

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and assigning symbols, titles, words and labels to classroom items and resources or personal possessions, such as meja, buku, komputer, and peta

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to stories, rhymes or songs, for example, Kancil dan Buaya, ‘Cicak-Cicak di Dinding’, Balonku ada Lima, and responding through movement, drawing and labelling or sequencing images to match the storyline or lyrics

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared reading of texts such as big books, and asking and answering questions about the text using contextual cues for support, for example, Pada hari Senin, si ulat makan apa?; Dia makan berapa stroberi?; Apakah si ulat lapar pada hari Jumat?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a class survey to write statements about self and others, for example, Tiga belas murid suka makan apel. Enam murid warna favoritnya hijau. Dua puluh murid hobinya bermain sepak bola.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to texts by sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that events occurred, or by creating a storyboard to retell a story or information

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating early literacy skills by labelling, matching, tracing, copying and drawing, for example, labelling items in the classroom, drawing a picture to match animal words, tracing colour words with the corresponding colour

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing themselves, a puppet or a toy with Nama saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using game-playing expressions (e.g. Selamat!; Saya menang!; Tidak apa-apa!; Kamu pandai!; Ayo main lagi!), then taking turns to lead a game, for example, Simon says: Bambang berkata angkat tangan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or soft toys to perform a dialogue, for example, Selamat siang, apa kabar?; Baik-baik saja, dan kamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a personal profile using modelled phrases to label pictures, for example, Umur saya tujuh tahun. Warna favorit saya merah. Saya suka makan nasi goreng dan bermain sepak bola

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing and giving descriptions of family members and pets, for example, Ini keluarga saya. Saya punya satu adik perempuan dan satu kakak laki-laki. Bapak saya pandai memasak. Anjing saya besar dan lucu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing what is entertaining or appealing in imaginative texts, for example, the characters, story or illustrations in books, songs, cartoons or comics such as Herman lucu; Saya suka si Kancil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating own version of a story by sequencing a series of pictures with captions or by creating a storyboard with labels using modelled language or by creating a different ending of a story, for example, Pada hari Senin, si ulat makan satu rambutan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing captions, with support, for a photographic display to show parents/others about a class event or experience (e.g. sports day, keeping a class pet, an excursion to the zoo), for example, Ini kelas kami di kolam renang; Ini marmot kelas kami, namanya Henry

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using secure digital tools to record and present a ‘show and tell’, for example, Ini kuda saya …; Makanan favorit dia …

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using mime and actions to demonstrate understanding, for example, miming a cat pose in response to the word kucing, responding to instructions such as duduk or berdiri with appropriate action, engaging in movement games such as jumping to a coloured spot, forming groups corresponding to teacher commands such as merah, tiga

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information in a spoken or written text to label, or draw a picture, for example, dia bermata biru

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images in catalogues, naming toys and games such as Kelereng Gundu, and selecting and listing items and prices

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and assigning symbols, titles, words and labels to classroom items and resources or personal possessions, such as meja, buku, komputer, and peta

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to stories, rhymes or songs, for example, Kancil dan Buaya, ‘Cicak-Cicak di Dinding’, Balonku ada Lima, and responding through movement, drawing and labelling or sequencing images to match the storyline or lyrics

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared reading of texts such as big books, and asking and answering questions about the text using contextual cues for support, for example, Pada hari Senin, si ulat makan apa?; Dia makan berapa stroberi?; Apakah si ulat lapar pada hari Jumat?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a class survey to write statements about self and others, for example, Tiga belas murid suka makan apel. Enam murid warna favoritnya hijau. Dua puluh murid hobinya bermain sepak bola.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to texts by sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that events occurred, or by creating a storyboard to retell a story or information

elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a range of games (e.g. matching pairs, filling in gaps, drag-and-drop, memory games, bingo), using secure digital tools and applications to reinforce vocabulary

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E02 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: following numerical notation to perform a collaborative musical piece on the angklung

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a treasure hunt finding objects related to colour, number, classroom items, for example, tiga buku merah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using familial terms of address in wider contexts, for example, Ibu/Bapak for teachers and adults

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages have loan words and that many Indonesian words are used in English (e.g. bamboo, orangutan, gecko, papaya) by creating a categories chart to list words from different languages, or playing a sorting game to sort words into their language of origin

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E09 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster to explain greetings at different times of the day (e.g. Selamat pagi; Selamat siang; Selamat sore; Selamat malam) and discussing the meaning of the word selamat

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating early literacy skills by labelling, matching, tracing, copying and drawing, for example, labelling items in the classroom, drawing a picture to match animal words, tracing colour words with the corresponding colour

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing themselves, a puppet or a toy with Nama saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using game-playing expressions (e.g. Selamat!; Saya menang!; Tidak apa-apa!; Kamu pandai!; Ayo main lagi!), then taking turns to lead a game, for example, Simon says: Bambang berkata angkat tangan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or soft toys to perform a dialogue, for example, Selamat siang, apa kabar?; Baik-baik saja, dan kamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a personal profile using modelled phrases to label pictures, for example, Umur saya tujuh tahun. Warna favorit saya merah. Saya suka makan nasi goreng dan bermain sepak bola

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing and giving descriptions of family members and pets, for example, Ini keluarga saya. Saya punya satu adik perempuan dan satu kakak laki-laki. Bapak saya pandai memasak. Anjing saya besar dan lucu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing what is entertaining or appealing in imaginative texts, for example, the characters, story or illustrations in books, songs, cartoons or comics such as Herman lucu; Saya suka si Kancil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating own version of a story by sequencing a series of pictures with captions or by creating a storyboard with labels using modelled language or by creating a different ending of a story, for example, Pada hari Senin, si ulat makan satu rambutan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing captions, with support, for a photographic display to show parents/others about a class event or experience (e.g. sports day, keeping a class pet, an excursion to the zoo), for example, Ini kelas kami di kolam renang; Ini marmot kelas kami, namanya Henry

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using secure digital tools to record and present a ‘show and tell’, for example, Ini kuda saya …; Makanan favorit dia …

elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting the Indonesian alphabet and/or singing alphabet rhymes/songs, and noticing that the Indonesian and English alphabets are both based on the Roman alphabet, but that the letters have different names in Indonesian and represent different sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: repeating words and phrases to imitate authentic Indonesian pronunciation, intonation and rhythm

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating Indonesian pronunciation, for example, vowels, trilled r, c (‘ch’) and the unaspirated sounds p, t and k especially at the end of a word (e.g. empat, nenek)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian has pure vowel sounds and each vowel sound is represented by one letter

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the vowel e has 3 different pronunciations: enam, sate, enak

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising diphthongs, for example, au in mau and ai in main

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: clapping the rhythm of syllables to notice even word stress

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that statements, commands and questions have different intonations

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting classmates and teacher, for example, Selamat pagi, Apa kabar? Baik, terima kasih.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for permission, for example, Boleh saya ke kamar kecil?, Boleh saya pinjam pensilmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using everyday Indonesian formulaic expressions, for example, Maaf; Permisi; Terima kasih; Silakan; Sama-sama; Ayo

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class, introducing themselves and responding to everyday personal questions such as Berapa umurmu? Di mana kamu tinggal? Apakah Anda punya hewan peliharaan?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming family members and friends and noticing the difference between the formal and informal forms, such as Ibu/Bu; Bapak/Pak; Nenek/Nek; Kakek/Kek; Adik/Dek

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and sharing simple expressions and songs with friends and family, for example, singing ‘Selamat ulang tahun’ and using appropriate greetings (e.g. Halo!; Selamat pagi / siang / sore / malam!) for different times or occasions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or printouts from popular shows or cartoons to role-play greetings and exchange information, imagining themselves as the character

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using PowerPoint slides or image flashcards to show different pictures (using taught vocabulary) to elicit responses

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple descriptive or expressive statements to describe themselves and to express their likes, preferences or feelings (e.g. Saya berusia lima tahun; Saya orang Australia; Saya suka olahraga; Saya lebih suka menari; Saya senang sekali), for example, creating a flipbook (on paper or digitally), drawing/pasting in images to support their sentences

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: generating phrases (e.g. Saya sedih; Saya sakit) using props such as images of faces with different expressions, for example, randomly distributing emoji faces attached to an icy pole stick and asking each student, Bagaimana keadaanmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to questions such as Apa ini/itu?, Ada berapa …?, Apa warna pensil ini? and Siapa ini?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing preferences such as choosing objects, for example, Saya mau … / Saya tidak mau … / Saya suka … / Saya kurang suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared performance of songs and chants with appropriate gestures, for example, ‘Kepala, Pundak, Lutut, Kaki’; Selamat Pagi, Pak. Selamat Pagi, Bu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-plays using modelled expressions and appropriate gestures in known scenarios such as introductions or shopping at a market, for example, Mau beli apa? Satu nanas dan dua pisang; Berapa harganya? Wah, mahal!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing number games (e.g. buzz and bingo), and using Indonesian to count places in dice games such as snakes and ladders

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing guessing games such as hot and cold or celebrity heads

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using nouns and pronouns to identify people, pets or things, for example, ibu, ayah, bapak, adik, kakak; anjing, kucing; buku, tas, pintu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying word order in familiar phrases to express possession, for example, nama saya …; ibu saya …; buku saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising prepositions of place, for example, di atas, di bawah, di dalam, di belakang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using base verbs to describe actions such as makan; duduk; minum; suka; tidur; bangun

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising auxiliary verbs such as mau, boleh, bisa and harus

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using high-frequency verbs in a variety of contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding question words and anticipating responses, for example, Siapa? (people); Apa? (objects, actions); Di mana? (location); Berapa? (quantity); Apakah? (yes/no responses)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cardinal numbers to count and in familiar phrases, for example, Umur saya tujuh tahun; Saya di kelas dua

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing a person, place or thing using noun+adjective phrases, for example, buku merah; anjing nakal; kucing lucu; bapak rajin; saya pendek; adik pandai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: joining words or phrases, using conjunctions such as dan, tetapi, juga and karena

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to things using demonstratives ini and itu, for example, Ini buku merah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negating verbs and adjectives using tidak and nouns using bukan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E01 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to questions such as Apa ini/itu?, Ada berapa …?, Apa warna pensil ini? and Siapa ini?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing preferences such as choosing objects, for example, Saya mau … / Saya tidak mau … / Saya suka … / Saya kurang suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared performance of songs and chants with appropriate gestures, for example, ‘Kepala, Pundak, Lutut, Kaki’; Selamat Pagi, Pak. Selamat Pagi, Bu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-plays using modelled expressions and appropriate gestures in known scenarios such as introductions or shopping at a market, for example, Mau beli apa? Satu nanas dan dua pisang; Berapa harganya? Wah, mahal!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing number games (e.g. buzz and bingo), and using Indonesian to count places in dice games such as snakes and ladders

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing guessing games such as hot and cold or celebrity heads

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2U04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken Indonesian has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing similarities in raising intonation at the end of questions and understanding the difference between statements, questions and exclamations

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing noun+adjective word order differences, for example, kucing hitam; mobil merah; bis besar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing difference in spontaneous exclamations in Indonesian and English, for example, Wah!; Aduh!, and sharing other examples from languages represented within the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian sentences use a subject+verb+object structure; noticing that this is similar to English sentences; and discussing similarities and differences with other known languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English represent cardinal numbers in the same way

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian forms plurals in different ways from English such as by duplicating, using a number or a qualifier, for example, kursi-kursi, dua kursi, banyak kursi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English divide the day differently, for example, comparing ‘good morning’ and ‘good afternoon’ with Selamat pagi and Selamat siang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in Indonesian siblings are identified in relation to position in the family, for example, kakak (older sibling), and discussing any other known languages that may identify family members in the same way

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that features of familiar texts may be similar or different in Indonesian and English, for example, the chorus of a song; the lines of a nursery rhyme or poem

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has some loan words from English (e.g. komputer, televisi), and that English has some from Indonesian (e.g. orangutan, satay, rambutan) with some changes in spelling, then noticing that some Australian English terms or expressions have no equivalent in Indonesian (e.g. koala, meat pie, farm), and that this is also the case with some Indonesian terms or expressions (e.g. becak, Kancil, mudik)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: tracing letters and simple words in both Indonesian and English, noticing similarities and differences

elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for permission, for example, Boleh saya ke kamar kecil?, Boleh saya pinjam pensilmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E06 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E07 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E08 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C01-E09 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that features of familiar texts may be similar or different in Indonesian and English, for example, the chorus of a song; the lines of a nursery rhyme or poem

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has some loan words from English (e.g. komputer, televisi), and that English has some from Indonesian (e.g. orangutan, satay, rambutan) with some changes in spelling, then noticing that some Australian English terms or expressions have no equivalent in Indonesian (e.g. koala, meat pie, farm), and that this is also the case with some Indonesian terms or expressions (e.g. becak, Kancil, mudik)

as_extracts.name: LINDF102-E12
as_extracts.description: They use common grammatical structures to create their own simple texts, with the support of visual and/or spoken cues.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: generating phrases (e.g. Saya sedih; Saya sakit) using props such as images of faces with different expressions, for example, randomly distributing emoji faces attached to an icy pole stick and asking each student, Bagaimana keadaanmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to questions such as Apa ini/itu?, Ada berapa …?, Apa warna pensil ini? and Siapa ini?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing preferences such as choosing objects, for example, Saya mau … / Saya tidak mau … / Saya suka … / Saya kurang suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared performance of songs and chants with appropriate gestures, for example, ‘Kepala, Pundak, Lutut, Kaki’; Selamat Pagi, Pak. Selamat Pagi, Bu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-plays using modelled expressions and appropriate gestures in known scenarios such as introductions or shopping at a market, for example, Mau beli apa? Satu nanas dan dua pisang; Berapa harganya? Wah, mahal!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing number games (e.g. buzz and bingo), and using Indonesian to count places in dice games such as snakes and ladders

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing guessing games such as hot and cold or celebrity heads

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2C05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating early literacy skills by labelling, matching, tracing, copying and drawing, for example, labelling items in the classroom, drawing a picture to match animal words, tracing colour words with the corresponding colour

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing themselves, a puppet or a toy with Nama saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using game-playing expressions (e.g. Selamat!; Saya menang!; Tidak apa-apa!; Kamu pandai!; Ayo main lagi!), then taking turns to lead a game, for example, Simon says: Bambang berkata angkat tangan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or soft toys to perform a dialogue, for example, Selamat siang, apa kabar?; Baik-baik saja, dan kamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a personal profile using modelled phrases to label pictures, for example, Umur saya tujuh tahun. Warna favorit saya merah. Saya suka makan nasi goreng dan bermain sepak bola

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing and giving descriptions of family members and pets, for example, Ini keluarga saya. Saya punya satu adik perempuan dan satu kakak laki-laki. Bapak saya pandai memasak. Anjing saya besar dan lucu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing what is entertaining or appealing in imaginative texts, for example, the characters, story or illustrations in books, songs, cartoons or comics such as Herman lucu; Saya suka si Kancil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating own version of a story by sequencing a series of pictures with captions or by creating a storyboard with labels using modelled language or by creating a different ending of a story, for example, Pada hari Senin, si ulat makan satu rambutan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing captions, with support, for a photographic display to show parents/others about a class event or experience (e.g. sports day, keeping a class pet, an excursion to the zoo), for example, Ini kelas kami di kolam renang; Ini marmot kelas kami, namanya Henry

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2C05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using secure digital tools to record and present a ‘show and tell’, for example, Ini kuda saya …; Makanan favorit dia …

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2U04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken Indonesian has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing similarities in raising intonation at the end of questions and understanding the difference between statements, questions and exclamations

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing noun+adjective word order differences, for example, kucing hitam; mobil merah; bis besar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing difference in spontaneous exclamations in Indonesian and English, for example, Wah!; Aduh!, and sharing other examples from languages represented within the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian sentences use a subject+verb+object structure; noticing that this is similar to English sentences; and discussing similarities and differences with other known languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English represent cardinal numbers in the same way

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian forms plurals in different ways from English such as by duplicating, using a number or a qualifier, for example, kursi-kursi, dua kursi, banyak kursi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English divide the day differently, for example, comparing ‘good morning’ and ‘good afternoon’ with Selamat pagi and Selamat siang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in Indonesian siblings are identified in relation to position in the family, for example, kakak (older sibling), and discussing any other known languages that may identify family members in the same way

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that features of familiar texts may be similar or different in Indonesian and English, for example, the chorus of a song; the lines of a nursery rhyme or poem

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has some loan words from English (e.g. komputer, televisi), and that English has some from Indonesian (e.g. orangutan, satay, rambutan) with some changes in spelling, then noticing that some Australian English terms or expressions have no equivalent in Indonesian (e.g. koala, meat pie, farm), and that this is also the case with some Indonesian terms or expressions (e.g. becak, Kancil, mudik)

as_extracts.name: LINDF102-E13
as_extracts.description: Students explore and recognise the influence of culture on language and identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2E04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Indonesian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing suit/suten/suwitan or hompimpa to decide who goes first in games

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing and engaging with cultural items from Indonesia, such as coins, postcards and authentic items

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: play-acting with dress-ups and props or with puppets when participating in role-plays

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected to various languages, cultures and traditions according to specific ethnic groups and regions in Indonesia, for example, in Javanese culture eating nasi tumpeng on celebratory occasions like birthdays or ketupat during Eid

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning Indonesian terms through the arts and culture, for example, topeng when making masks, batik when making modified batik art, wayang when playing with leather puppets

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring similarities and differences in onomatopoeia in Indonesian and other languages represented in the classroom, for example, gong-gong (woof, woof), meong (miaow), kwek-kwek (quack, quack), cit-cit (tweet, tweet), hacciihh (achoo) and kring-kring (ding, ding)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2U05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how Indonesian-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing with the class words and phrases they know in other languages and cultures, for example, greetings, numbers

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring food words and their origins, for example, nasi goreng, sushi, lasagne

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that words reflect aspects of culture, for example, main bola compared to ‘play footy’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that Indonesian primary school uniforms are red and white, comparing with the colours of the Indonesian flag, learning that the flag is named Sang Merah Putih, and discussing the representation of colours in different cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with celebrations in Indonesian-speaking communities (e.g. traditions, customs, costumes, food), and noticing similarities and differences with celebrations in their own communities

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying symbols and colours used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and by Indonesian-speaking communities in a range of contexts, for example, identifying the colours on a range of flags from different countries and communities in Indonesian, and discussing what the colours represent in English

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making their own bilingual/picture dictionaries, captions, signs, labels and descriptions to convey cultural references such as mandi, guling, kakak, adik, sepak takraw, durian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing and recognising that ways of greeting and addressing others may change according to cultural norms such as using respectful forms of address, culturally appropriate gestures and expected formalities in the Indonesian classroom, for example, taking leave from the teacher at the end of the lesson (e.g. Terima kasih Pak/Bu; Sampai jumpa besok; Selamat siang)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages and communities have different protocols regarding the use of terms of respect, for example, there are ways of addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using familial terms (e.g. Uncle, Aunty) depending on the relationship, and comparing these terms with those in Indonesian and/or other languages

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring different cultural practices and related language use through games, for example, suit/suten/suwitan or hompimpa bekel

as_extracts.name: LINDF102-E14
as_extracts.description: They recognise that Indonesian is spoken in communities and regions in Australia and around the world, and relate this to their own language(s) and culture(s).

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN2U06 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: identify where Indonesian is used around the world and recognise that there are many different languages spoken in communities throughout Australia
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U06-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating Indonesia, Australia and countries/places of significance to students in the class, on a digital or print world map

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U06-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesia is a country made up of thousands of islands with many different cultures, and that most Indonesians speak regional languages as well as the national Indonesian language, Bahasa Indonesia

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2U06-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing some key words in Indonesian with Malay languages spoken in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei, for example, numbers, greetings

elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian uses the Roman alphabet like English, but noticing that some of the sounds are different

elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a video clip of Indonesian children at school and discussing what they notice

elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing information about the language(s) they speak at home, for example, Saya berbicara bahasa Italia

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the different languages spoken by members of the class, and listening to the different sounds and ways of saying common expressions such as ‘Good morning’ or ‘My name is …’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing songs such as an Indonesian alphabet song, counting songs or songs focusing on specific sounds or repetition

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing songs, rhymes and action stories, using non-verbal forms of expression such as gestures, facial expressions and body language to support understanding

elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting the teacher in Indonesian, when their name is called on the roll or through choral class greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in songs and chants, for example, ‘Topi Saya Bundar’, ‘Lingkaran Kecil Lingkaran Besar’ and ‘Satu Satu Aku Sayang Ibu’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous Indonesian exclamations when interacting with peers, for example, Aduh!; Wah!; Bagus!; Hebat!; Hati-hati!

elaborations.elaboration_text: clapping the number of syllables in common words as they say them, for example, clapping the syllables in greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing bingo with images, sounds, words or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising short tongue twisters or rhymes

elaborations.name: VC2LIN2E02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring sounds with onomatopoeia, for example, learning the sounds of different animals
