elaborations.elaboration_text: naming family members and friends and noticing the difference between the formal and informal forms, such as Ibu/Bu; Bapak/Pak; Nenek/Nek; Kakek/Kek; Adik/Dek

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, Indonesian language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers through purposeful and creative play in structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They use Indonesian to interact with their peers and teachers and to participate in activities in familiar settings that reflect their interests and capabilities. They use local and digital resources to explore Indonesian-speaking communities. They continue to receive extensive support through modelling, scaffolding and repetition, as well as the use of targeted resources. 

Students develop active listening skills and use gestures, words and modelled expressions, imitating the sounds, pronunciation and intonation of Indonesian. They locate information, and respond to and create texts using written and spoken Indonesian. They access authentic and purpose-developed Indonesian-language texts such as picture books, stories, songs, digital and animated games, timetables, recipes and advertisements. They recognise the interconnected nature of language, culture and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 4, students use Indonesian to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds. They use modelled language to participate in spoken and written activities. They locate and respond to key items of information in texts, using strategies to help interpret and convey meaning in familiar contexts. They use modelled language and basic grammatical structures to create texts.

Students imitate the sound combinations and rhythms of spoken Indonesian. They demonstrate their understanding that Indonesian has non-verbal, spoken and written language conventions and rules to convey meaning. They recognise that some terms have cultural meanings. They identify patterns in Indonesian and make comparisons between Indonesian and English, using simple metalanguage. They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4C01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E01 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E03 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making and responding to requests, for example, Boleh pinjam …?, and asking for rephrasing, repetition and clarification, for example, Maaf Bu/Pak, apa artinya …?; Boleh tolong ulangi sekali lagi?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronouns and adjectives of character and appearance to describe people and animals, for example, Ini bapak saya. Dia tinggi dan baik hati.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using possessive word order to describe objects related to home, school and local environment, for example, Kota saya kecil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to describe position, for example, Ada monyet di atas meja; and prepositions dengan and untuk, for example, Jus ini untuk siapa? Untuk saya!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing actions using base verbs such as tinggal, bangun, mandi, naik and ber verbs, for example, bermain, berjalan, bersepeda, berenang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using questions when presenting a role-play, for example, Siapa …?; Apa?; Di mana?; Berapa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking ideas using conjunctions, for example, dan, karena, tetapi, atau, dengan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating events in time using adverbs, for example, hari ini, kemarin, besok, sudah, belum

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising language features associated with texts such as sequencing phrases, for example, Pertama-tama … lalu … akhirnya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ordinal numbers (e.g. pertama, kedua), and using cardinal numbers in a range of contexts such as arithmetic or saying prices, for example, Saya anak ketiga di keluarga saya; Satu tambah dua sama dengan tiga; Harganya lima ribu rupiah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the connection between spelling convention and meaning in duplicated verbs expressing leisurely action, for example, comparing melihat with melihat-lihat; berjalan with jalan-jalan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that subject+verb+object sentence construction is similar in Indonesian and English but Indonesian verbs do not change depending on tense, for example, saya makan nasi kemarin; saya suka makan nasi; saya sedang makan nasi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the verb ‘to be’ is implied when linked to a noun phrase, adjective or prepositional phrase, for example, Saya murid; Saya tinggi; Buku di laci

content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information about activities of others such as surveying peers about time spent on activities and presenting the results to the class, for example, Berapa jam kamu menonton televisi / membaca buku / bermain komputer / bermain olahraga / makan / belajar / tidur? Kamu naik apa ke sekolah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to information in texts about aspects of culture such as lifestyle, diet or use of transport, for example, Dia naik apa ke sekolah? Dia naik …; Dan kamu? Saya naik …; Mereka makan apa untuk sarapan / makan malam? Mereka makan …; Dan kamu? Kadang-kadang saya makan …; Kamu lebih suka … atau …? Saya lebih suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing information about activities and practices of a school in Indonesia with those of their own school, for example, listening to, reading or viewing texts related to aspects of school life such as timetables, canteen menus, extracurricular activities and sports, and making a Venn diagram or infographic

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: working collaboratively to obtain and use information from texts related to other learning areas, for example, following instructions for a simple science experiment or skill-building in Health and Physical Education such as Pertama-tama kita harus …; Lompat tiga kali; Letakkan tangan di belakang kepala; Lempar bola ke keranjang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing texts and responding to questions about characters, ideas and events in Indonesian or English, for example, Kamu paling suka karakter siapa? Mengapa? Apakah … merasa senang sesudah bertemu temannya? Mengapa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to imaginative texts by expressing personal opinions about and reactions to the characters or plot, for example, Tokoh favorit saya Sinta karena dia cantik; Saya pikir Arjuna hebat karena dia berani dan pandai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an imaginative text and demonstrating understanding by performing a role-play or illustrating and captioning aspects of the plot

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an informative text about topics such as geography or arts and crafts by answering true-or-false questions, completing crossword puzzles or by creating their own questions for a trivia quiz

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing the use of forms of address in exchanges and comparing their presence or absence in equivalent exchanges in English or other languages spoken by the students, for example, Silakan makan Ibu; Duduk sini, kak; Bapak mau ke mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of kinship words for terms of address (e.g. Bapak, Ibu, Kak, Dik) and comparing with other cultures, then discussing the connection between culture and naming systems, for example, Balinese birth order for names

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring how gestures differ between cultures, for example, Indonesian people beckon with palm down and moving all fingers, and practising using culturally appropriate gestures in the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing their own ‘family culture’ with that of peers and considering how family culture can impact on identity, offering reasons for similarities and differences, for example, comparing different ways in which birthdays are celebrated

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring appropriate etiquette in different contexts and cultures and participating in interactions associated with Indonesian practices, for example, waiting for the host to say Silakan makan and using the right hand to eat

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place on which they live and incorporating this into their self-introduction in Indonesian

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the exchange of terms between Indonesian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages such as the use of Makassan terms in Yolngu, for example, balanda, rupiah, nenek

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are regional differences in language and cultural practices throughout Indonesia (e.g. Mbak and Mas as terms of address in Javanese-speaking communities) and discussing how Australian terms and expressions might be understood from an Indonesian perspective, for example, ‘bushwalking’, ‘kick a footy’, ‘no worries’ or ‘BBQing’

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1

organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing awareness that language carries cultural ideas that may have no direct equivalent in English (e.g. upacara compared with ‘assembly’, padi/beras/nasi compared with ‘cooked/uncooked rice’, and kaki lima/warung compared with ‘food carts/food stalls’), or noticing how their Indonesian language learning has enriched their understanding of ‘untranslatable terms’, for example, using becak in English language conversation

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying character traits and values in Indonesian stories, for example, Kancil stories feature animals native to Indonesia, and comparing these with familiar Australian stories such as Diary of a Wombat

elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how own language influences expectations about Indonesian language, for example, perceiving word order as ‘back-to-front’ compared with English; wanting to use one word for ‘you’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising features of a simple spoken or written text in Indonesian (e.g. a verbal greeting or a written message), for example, noting terms of address and ways of signing off, and comparing them with similar texts in English

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying examples of how Indonesian has influenced Australian English, for example, sarong, satay, batik, orangutan, nasi goreng, and playing word-find games with these words

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian uses affixes to change parts of speech, for example, kolam renang and berenang; sepeda and bersepeda; makan and makanan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and explaining expressions which do not easily translate into English, for example, Sudah mandi?; Makan di warung; Selamat jalan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing parts of a sentence using metalanguage (e.g. noun, verb, adverb, adjective) to describe words, and noticing the word order and patterns

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some words originate from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages from different areas around Australia, for example, dingo (dingo) from the Dharug word din-gu, and comparing these words to English and/or other languages and discussing their historical context

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

as_extracts.name: LINDF104-E09
as_extracts.description: They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4U04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: identify connections between personal identity, language and aspects of culture
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of kinship words for terms of address (e.g. Bapak, Ibu, Kak, Dik) and comparing with other cultures, then discussing the connection between culture and naming systems, for example, Balinese birth order for names

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring how gestures differ between cultures, for example, Indonesian people beckon with palm down and moving all fingers, and practising using culturally appropriate gestures in the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing their own ‘family culture’ with that of peers and considering how family culture can impact on identity, offering reasons for similarities and differences, for example, comparing different ways in which birthdays are celebrated

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring appropriate etiquette in different contexts and cultures and participating in interactions associated with Indonesian practices, for example, waiting for the host to say Silakan makan and using the right hand to eat

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place on which they live and incorporating this into their self-introduction in Indonesian

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the exchange of terms between Indonesian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages such as the use of Makassan terms in Yolngu, for example, balanda, rupiah, nenek

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are regional differences in language and cultural practices throughout Indonesia (e.g. Mbak and Mas as terms of address in Javanese-speaking communities) and discussing how Australian terms and expressions might be understood from an Indonesian perspective, for example, ‘bushwalking’, ‘kick a footy’, ‘no worries’ or ‘BBQing’

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing awareness that language carries cultural ideas that may have no direct equivalent in English (e.g. upacara compared with ‘assembly’, padi/beras/nasi compared with ‘cooked/uncooked rice’, and kaki lima/warung compared with ‘food carts/food stalls’), or noticing how their Indonesian language learning has enriched their understanding of ‘untranslatable terms’, for example, using becak in English language conversation

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying character traits and values in Indonesian stories, for example, Kancil stories feature animals native to Indonesia, and comparing these with familiar Australian stories such as Diary of a Wombat

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4C01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions about themselves related to daily routine, family and friends, pastimes and aspects of school and home, for example, Saya tinggal di Geelong dengan keluarga saya; Rumah saya besar; Saya bermain bola basket; Saya suka es krim; Saya berasal dari …; Saya berumur … tahun; Saya anggota klub …; Saya anak ke … di keluarga saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in class routines such as asking and answering the question Apa kabar? and follow-up questions such as Ada apa? with their teacher and classmates at the start of a lesson

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing feelings with others using modelled language, for example, Saya merasa sedih karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making and responding to requests, for example, Boleh pinjam …?, and asking for rephrasing, repetition and clarification, for example, Maaf Bu/Pak, apa artinya …?; Boleh tolong ulangi sekali lagi?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using kinship terms and names in place of personal pronouns, for example, using Bapak and Ibu for ‘you’ and ‘your’ when speaking to adults, using a person’s name instead of kamu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions, for example, when selecting dress-ups for an activity, Mau yang mana? (Saya mau) yang biru. Kamu lebih suka yang mana? (Saya lebih suka) yang pendek

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing a game while playing, for example, Siapa mau mulai?; Giliran siapa? Giliran saya; Sally menang!; Hebat!; Bagus!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple correspondence with peers, such as notes, invitations or birthday cards in print or digital form

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4C02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate gestures, for example, bending and saying permisi when passing someone, responding to Di mana …? by pointing appropriately

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to preparing and displaying a set of class rules, for example, Jangan berlari di ruang kelas

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: praising each other (e.g. Hebat!; Luar biasa!; Bagus sekali!; Salut!) when working collaboratively with the class on tasks that require following instructions such as cooking or other step-based activities such as crafts or drawing tasks

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in group activities such as role-plays, and asking and responding to questions and invitations, for example, Mau ke mana?; Mau ikut?; Mau beli apa?; Saya mau beli dua kilo apel

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating with others to make decisions such as choosing the menu for a class party, for example, Berapa paket kentang goreng? Sepuluh! Jangan! Lima cukup!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating wayang puppets and discussing character traits and appearance in preparation for a collaborative performance, for example, Wayang saya bernama …; Apakah wayang kamu sportif? Wah, wayangmu berhidung besar!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a description of an imaginary creature for another student to draw, for example, Dia punya satu mata dan dua mulut. Dia berhidung besar dan rambutnya panjang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a treasure hunt, developing instructions and giving and following directions, for example, Dari pintu belok ke kiri, jalan terus sampai meja guru

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing, rehearsing and presenting an Indonesian-themed item at the school assembly

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: working collaboratively and sharing decisions about content and vocabulary when designing a poster for a specific event, creating a picture book or word wall, for example, Saya pikir …; Lebih baik …

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4C03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate and respond to key information related to familiar content obtained from spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information about activities of others such as surveying peers about time spent on activities and presenting the results to the class, for example, Berapa jam kamu menonton televisi / membaca buku / bermain komputer / bermain olahraga / makan / belajar / tidur? Kamu naik apa ke sekolah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to information in texts about aspects of culture such as lifestyle, diet or use of transport, for example, Dia naik apa ke sekolah? Dia naik …; Dan kamu? Saya naik …; Mereka makan apa untuk sarapan / makan malam? Mereka makan …; Dan kamu? Kadang-kadang saya makan …; Kamu lebih suka … atau …? Saya lebih suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing information about activities and practices of a school in Indonesia with those of their own school, for example, listening to, reading or viewing texts related to aspects of school life such as timetables, canteen menus, extracurricular activities and sports, and making a Venn diagram or infographic

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: working collaboratively to obtain and use information from texts related to other learning areas, for example, following instructions for a simple science experiment or skill-building in Health and Physical Education such as Pertama-tama kita harus …; Lompat tiga kali; Letakkan tangan di belakang kepala; Lempar bola ke keranjang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing texts and responding to questions about characters, ideas and events in Indonesian or English, for example, Kamu paling suka karakter siapa? Mengapa? Apakah … merasa senang sesudah bertemu temannya? Mengapa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to imaginative texts by expressing personal opinions about and reactions to the characters or plot, for example, Tokoh favorit saya Sinta karena dia cantik; Saya pikir Arjuna hebat karena dia berani dan pandai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an imaginative text and demonstrating understanding by performing a role-play or illustrating and captioning aspects of the plot

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an informative text about topics such as geography or arts and crafts by answering true-or-false questions, completing crossword puzzles or by creating their own questions for a trivia quiz

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing the use of forms of address in exchanges and comparing their presence or absence in equivalent exchanges in English or other languages spoken by the students, for example, Silakan makan Ibu; Duduk sini, kak; Bapak mau ke mana?

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4C04 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce Indonesian, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using texts such as public signs to understand meaning and context and adapting to their own environment, for example, changing Awas gajah! to Awas kangguru! Hati-hati banyak sepeda motor! Hati-hati banyak mobil!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting and using Indonesian words and expressions that do not translate easily into English, for example, kaki lima; warung; Kamu anak keberapa di keluargamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a glossary or word bank of common Indonesian expressions and idioms that convey Indonesian cultural practices

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using multimodal resources to compile customised word banks that they can use when talking about areas of personal interest

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using contextual clues to predict meaning in familiar text types (e.g. sound effects in a comic; background visuals in a song video; layout of an invitation) and adapting to create their own texts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to informative and imaginative print and digital books, short-scripted plays, or animations that use familiar Indonesian words, by creating a class display of the key information and providing a glossary of new words and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use print and online dictionaries to look up unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a familiar story, writing or acting out a plausible different ending, and using new words, expressions and gestures to convey the key messages of the story

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4C05 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing modelled texts, for example, creating a storyboard using pictures and captions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic expressions to create a personalised greeting card such as a birthday card or Idul Fitri card designing Indonesian signs and instructions in the classroom and around the school, for example, Cuci tangan; Tong sampah; Selamat datang di sekolah kami

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information such as a display or slideshow about home, school and local environment, for example, rumah saya di …; Di sekolah kami ada …; Kota kami adalah …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a series of simulated diary entries using modelled language to talk about their personal worlds and express own ideas, for example, Pada hari Sabtu keluarga saya berenang di …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a self-introduction for a character and using digital tools to link the recording to an image or video, for example, Kenalkan, nama saya …, saya terkenal karena saya bisa …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing a text and creating a profile of the main characters, for example, Rama kuat dan berani. Dia suami Sinta

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing a role-play scenario associated with Indonesian practices such as using appropriate language and gestures at a meal, for example, Silakan makan, tambah lagi and using the right hand when serving tea, or paying for stamps at the post office

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using different text types (e.g. postcards, emails), styles of writing (e.g. informative, persuasive, imaginative) and the specific language conventions associated with them

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a new version of a known imaginative text, for example, adding characters; changing setting; composing a different ending

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4C05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing a play for classmates or the wider school community using wayang puppets made in class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4U01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise sound combinations, and use patterns of pronunciation and intonation to form words, phrases and simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an alphabet bank, collecting words that begin with each letter (e.g. Aku/apa/apel, bagaimana/beruang/buaya/burung, cacing/cicak)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using Indonesian pronunciation for trilled r, c (‘ch’), u (as in ‘put’), a (as in ‘aqua’), e (as in ‘egg’) and unaspirated sounds p, t and k when reading aloud from written text

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing aa sound, for example, maaf, saat and words from Arabic, for example, Jumat (Jum’at)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating Indonesian pronunciation of initial ny sounds, for example, nyamuk, Nyoman

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising different intonation for statements and questions, for example, Kamu suka apel (with falling intonation) and Kamu suka apel? (with rising intonation)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising imperatives, for example, Angkat tangan!; Buka bukumu!; Ayo cepat!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying onomatopoeic words such as those related to transport, for example, tut-tut (‘toot toot’ – car horn), brum-brum (‘brum brum’ – motorcycle), jes-jes (‘choo choo’ – puffing train), kring-kring (‘ding ding’ – bike bell)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4U02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use modelled language, formulaic phrases, simple grammatical structures and language conventions to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronouns and adjectives of character and appearance to describe people and animals, for example, Ini bapak saya. Dia tinggi dan baik hati.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using possessive word order to describe objects related to home, school and local environment, for example, Kota saya kecil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to describe position, for example, Ada monyet di atas meja; and prepositions dengan and untuk, for example, Jus ini untuk siapa? Untuk saya!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing actions using base verbs such as tinggal, bangun, mandi, naik and ber verbs, for example, bermain, berjalan, bersepeda, berenang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using questions when presenting a role-play, for example, Siapa …?; Apa?; Di mana?; Berapa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking ideas using conjunctions, for example, dan, karena, tetapi, atau, dengan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating events in time using adverbs, for example, hari ini, kemarin, besok, sudah, belum

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising language features associated with texts such as sequencing phrases, for example, Pertama-tama … lalu … akhirnya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ordinal numbers (e.g. pertama, kedua), and using cardinal numbers in a range of contexts such as arithmetic or saying prices, for example, Saya anak ketiga di keluarga saya; Satu tambah dua sama dengan tiga; Harganya lima ribu rupiah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the connection between spelling convention and meaning in duplicated verbs expressing leisurely action, for example, comparing melihat with melihat-lihat; berjalan with jalan-jalan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that subject+verb+object sentence construction is similar in Indonesian and English but Indonesian verbs do not change depending on tense, for example, saya makan nasi kemarin; saya suka makan nasi; saya sedang makan nasi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the verb ‘to be’ is implied when linked to a noun phrase, adjective or prepositional phrase, for example, Saya murid; Saya tinggi; Buku di laci

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN4U03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and compare familiar Indonesian language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using simple metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian and English have the same punctuation rules, for example, using capital letters and full stops for sentences and identifying these in sentences or short texts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising similarities and differences between Indonesian, English and/or other languages in ways of showing politeness, for example, making requests and expressing gratitude, Tolong/Silakan …; Terima kasih. Boleh saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how own language influences expectations about Indonesian language, for example, perceiving word order as ‘back-to-front’ compared with English; wanting to use one word for ‘you’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising features of a simple spoken or written text in Indonesian (e.g. a verbal greeting or a written message), for example, noting terms of address and ways of signing off, and comparing them with similar texts in English

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying examples of how Indonesian has influenced Australian English, for example, sarong, satay, batik, orangutan, nasi goreng, and playing word-find games with these words

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian uses affixes to change parts of speech, for example, kolam renang and berenang; sepeda and bersepeda; makan and makanan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and explaining expressions which do not easily translate into English, for example, Sudah mandi?; Makan di warung; Selamat jalan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing parts of a sentence using metalanguage (e.g. noun, verb, adverb, adjective) to describe words, and noticing the word order and patterns

elaborations.name: VC2LIN4U03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some words originate from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages from different areas around Australia, for example, dingo (dingo) from the Dharug word din-gu, and comparing these words to English and/or other languages and discussing their historical context

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 5 and 6, Indonesian language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers in purposeful, creative and structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They interact in Indonesian to exchange information and ideas within their school and local environment, and engage with Indonesian-speaking communities. They work independently and in groups, with ongoing support from modelling and from digital and print resources. 

Students engage with a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts that may include stories, posters, images, notes, invitations, video clips and procedural texts. They identify language structures and features of Indonesian and use simple metalanguage to reflect on their understanding. They recognise that some words and expressions are not easily translated, and reflect on how diverse cultural practices, behaviours and values influence communication and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 6, students initiate and use strategies to maintain interactions in Indonesian that are related to their immediate environment. They use appropriate sound combinations, intonation and rhythm in spoken texts. They collaborate in spoken and written activities to share information, preferences and ideas. They use strategies to locate and interpret information and ideas in texts, and demonstrate understanding by responding in Indonesian or English, adjusting their responses to context, purpose and audience.

Students use modelled structures when creating and responding in Indonesian. They create texts, selecting and using a variety of vocabulary and sentence structures to suit different contexts. They use conventions appropriate to text type. They apply rules for pronunciation and intonation in spoken language and apply conventions of spelling and punctuation in written language. They compare language structures and features in Indonesian and English, using familiar metalanguage. They show understanding of how language and culture are interconnected and consider how this is reflected in their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending subject-focus construction by adding a preposition or adverb to subject+verb+object word order, for example, Saya menonton film di bioskop; Pada hari Minggu saya berselancar dengan bapak di pantai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using affixation to form possessive pronouns, for example, -nya, -mu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to describe location and follow directions, for example, Belok ke kiri di depan gereja; Kolam renang ada di antara bioskop dan taman

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to relationships between people and things using prepositions, for example, buku in untuk …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing actions using me- verbs, for example, menonton, melihat, menjual, mendengarkan, membeli, memakai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: directing others using imperatives, for example, Jangan duduk di atas meja, Dilarang masuk; using polite forms -lah, Silakan, for example, Diamlah! Silakan duduk

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using question words to seek information or explanation, for example, Berapa lama?; Untuk apa?; Dengan siapa?; Dengan apa?; Yang mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating time and tense using adverbs, for example, tadi pagi; nanti sore; pada hari Senin; sekarang; yang lalu; yang akan datang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing frequency using adverbs, for example, selalu, sering, kadang-kadang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating cohesion using conjunctions, for example, lalu, sebelum, sesudah, sesudah itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using comparatives and superlatives, for example, lebih … daripada; paling …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing games such as matching pairs to reinforce grammatical rules, for example, matching nouns and subject pronouns

as_extracts.name: LINDF106-E09
as_extracts.description: They compare language structures and features in Indonesian and English, using familiar metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN6C04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in Indonesian in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of tools such as dictionaries and online translators to effectively assist interpretation of meaning in context, for example, checking meaning of word(s) that may have multiple meanings (e.g. the English word ‘see’) and choosing the correct word for the context

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing texts in Indonesian and English and discussing similarities and differences, for example, menus may have words and phrases from other languages; procedural texts are often presented as ordered lists

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing translations of written texts, such as advertisements and food packaging, from Indonesian into English and from English into Indonesian, and considering how meanings may be interpreted from a different cultural perspective

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing creative texts and discussing key points such as a quality of a character or special features of the plot, for example, Cerita menarik karena …; Pada pendapat saya tokoh itu kurang jujur karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting meanings in Indonesian texts by ‘reading’ the context (including non-verbal cues), for example, interpreting the phrase Ayo cepat! as encouraging or scolding, depending on context and body language

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting aspects of spoken texts in Indonesian, for example, providing a bilingual spoken or written commentary for an Indonesian item at a school assembly

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using drawings or animations to explain the meanings of idiomatic expressions, for example, masuk angin; jam karet

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing bilingual versions of an imaginative text, noticing any differences, and explaining why particular language may have been added or omitted and how the meaning may have changed

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating bilingual texts for the school community, for example, a virtual tour for a school website or location signs within the school

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing a role-play for a specific audience such as parents or younger students and providing a bilingual commentary, for example, explaining the use of specific terms or gestures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN6U03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: compare Indonesian language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing language use in similar social situations in Indonesian and English, for example, Wkwkwk and LOL in text messaging; salutations in emails and letters

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian is influenced by other languages and cultures, for example, wortel (Dutch), bakso (Chinese), kriket (English), magrib (Arabic), agama (Sanskrit)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the use of loan words from other languages in texts such as advertisements and popular music to suggest values such as ‘modern’, ‘sophisticated’ and ‘educated’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that word order, rather than word form, determines personal and possessive pronouns, for example, saya guru and guru saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that ‘please’ in English has a different Indonesian equivalent depending on context, for example, silakan, tolong, coba

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing understanding of how different text types use linguistic features to create effects, for example, superlatives in advertisements designed to persuade (terbaru, paling sehat), the imperative in signs designed to advise or prohibit (Dilarang), salutations in emails designed to maintain relationships (yang baik, salam dari)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the forms used for giving instructions vary depending on the social situation, for example, Duduk; Duduklah; Silakan duduk

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how different degrees of formality are expressed when making requests, for example, Minta; Mohon; Boleh minta …; Bolehkah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: talking about grammar, using metalanguage such as pronouns, identifying language elements, and talking about how they are used

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U03-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage to discuss the features of familiar texts, for example, a shopping list serves as a reminder; a role-play at a market involves interaction and negotiation; an email or text message to a friend involves interaction and an exchange of information

as_extracts.name: LINDF106-E10
as_extracts.description: They show understanding of how language and culture are interconnected and consider how this is reflected in their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN6U04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity, and that this has an impact on verbal and non-verbal communication
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the impact of gestures across cultures, for example, beckoning by pointing with index finger or with palm down, touching the top of the head or laughing loudly, and noticing their own comfort with these

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing ways of showing politeness, for example, avoiding giving a negative answer as a way of saving face, or softening negatives by using belum or kurang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that their language use reflects their own cultural perspective and experiences, for example, ‘school camp’, ‘the bush’, ‘footy’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing the position and/or location of Indonesia in Indonesian compared with the lands of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples in northern Australia on a map of Australasia

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and/or listening to Indonesian folktales and considering similarities and differences with Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ stories, for example, comparing the legend of the Bali Strait with Gundijtmara stories explaining the formation of the Budj Bim landscape

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the exchange of terms between Indonesian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages such as the use of Makassan terms in Yolngu, for example, balanda, rupiah, nenek

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how regional language, ethnic group and religious affiliation can influence use of Indonesian language, for example, Mbak and Mas as terms of address in Java, Assalamualaikum in greetings (especially for Muslim Indonesians), Selamat Hari Paskah (for Catholic and Christian Indonesians)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian as a national language enables communication across diverse groups of people and languages, and is part of national identity

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on what they have learnt about Indonesian cultures through learning Indonesian and noticing how their assumptions might have changed

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6U04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring examples of traditional and contemporary images or texts in print and online, and discussing how identity and gender are represented in the language

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN6C01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to their personal worlds and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions about aspects of their personal worlds such as likes and dislikes, interests and leisure activities, for example, Saya lebih suka bermain bola basket daripada sepak bola

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: agreeing or disagreeing politely with other opinions when discussing important topics related to the school environment and their personal worlds, for example, Saya setuju/tidak setuju; Saya suka/tidak/kurang suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information about significant people such as family members, friends and teachers, and describing their relationship, physical appearance and characteristics/qualities, for example, Teman saya baik hati dan lucu; Dia bermata biru dan rambutnya merah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recounting experiences with family and friends, for example, Pada hari Sabtu, saya berbelanja di pasar dengan teman. Saya membeli …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting a simulated interview with someone they consider a role model such as a sports figure, a musician, artist, teacher, family or friend, for example, Kapan kamu mulai suka berselancar?; Siapa membantu kamu berlatih gitar?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging emails with a real or imagined Indonesian student of similar age, under teacher supervision

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using strategies such as asking questions, fillers and interjections to sustain interactions with others, for example, Oh begitu!; Maaf?; Dan kamu?; Saya setuju!; Terus …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions, and asking for repetition or clarification, for example, Sekali lagi, Bu; Maaf, Pak, saya tidak mengerti; Tolong lebih pelan!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking permission, for example, Boleh saya ke kamar kecil?; Boleh pinjam kamus/penggaris/pena merah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C01-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and participating in role-plays that replicate everyday situations such as purchasing pastries in a bakery, requesting information about train or bus schedules, or asking for directions to a place in town

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN6C02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve discussion with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising displays, presentations or performances for family, friends or the school community to showcase their progress in learning and using Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in class activities and games, for example, Mau ikut tim kami?; Giliran siapa sekarang?; Bagaimana kalau kita …; Ayo mulai!; Mari kita bermain …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving advice and reminders to peers, for example, Pakailah sepatumu; Kamu harus menulis di bukumu; Jangan berbicara keras; Lebih baik kamu belajar sekarang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in and adapting scenarios related to purchasing goods and services such as bargaining scenarios, buying souvenirs or ordering food at a kaki lima/warung, for example, Boleh saya minta nasi goreng dan teh manis; Minta bonnya; Berapa harga baju batik itu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in shared tasks which involve planning, collaborating and evaluating, for example, planning a real or imagined visit to a location, then acting as tour guides for their classmates in simulated scenarios

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making print or digital invitations and arrangements for a shared event or experience such as a class party, an Indonesian visitor or a film afternoon

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning a real or imagined trip to Indonesia, agreeing on itinerary and packing list, for example, Bagaimana kalau kita ke Yogyakarta? Saya mau mengunjungi Borobudur; Sebaiknya kita membawa apa? Tidak perlu membawa jaket karena di Indonesia cuaca panas

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information to organise a meeting with friends, discussing where and when it will take place, for example, Kita kumpul di mana?; Maaf saya tidak bisa pada hari Jumat; Bagaimana kalau hari Sabtu jam 10 pagi?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and organising a performance item for school assembly showcasing what they have learnt in their Indonesian class, allocating roles and negotiating with class members (e.g. who will recite a poem, who will sing, who will perform a rap, who will perform a role-play), for example, Saya mau bernyanyi. Siapa yang mau berdansa?; Kita akan berlatih sesudah makan siang di depan kantin

strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN6C03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to instructions and commands, for example, Masuk!; Buka laptop kamu!; Jangan lari!; Tulis di bukumu!; Baca lebih keras!; Maju ke depan!; Dengarkan!; Ulangi!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to questions about main characters and events in texts, for example, Siapa?; Di mana?; Berapa lama?; Apa?; Kapan?; Bagaimana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: conveying understanding of plot and sequence in texts such as recreating the sequence using a storyboard, labelling key events or creating a timeline

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing texts and extracting key points about an issue or topic, for example, watching a video about Indonesian Independence Day activities and writing a recount of events using modelled phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information about activities and their environment to share with others, for example, making a short documentary about their neighbourhood/region to present to students at a sister school in Indonesia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in texts such as advertisements, conversations, brochures and announcements, and sharing this information with others in another format, for example, watching a range of advertisements and exchanging opinions about which one they liked best and why

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and comparing perspectives about information in spoken and written texts, for example, Apakah informasi ini benar?; Informasi ini dari mana?; Siapa yang menulis teks ini?; Berapa orang setuju?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the history of trade, economic and/or cultural connections between Indonesians and Australians, for example, developing a multimodal presentation to explain the history of contact between Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples from northern Australia and Indonesians through the trepang fishing trade

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching cultural activities and events of significance in Indonesian-speaking communities and comparing with their own experience, for example, daily routines, celebrations, sporting events

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C03-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: documenting information found through their own or group research, for example, facts about city versus village life in Indonesia documented through captioned images, charts and/or an oral presentation

substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using graphic organisers to convey information in different ways, for example, to show priorities (list/table), to compare statistics or ideas (Venn diagram), or to highlight frequency (graphs)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing texts for their own and others’ enjoyment and interest, for example, describing an imaginary character, animal or event

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and presenting a poem, song or rap, experimenting with rhyme and rhythm

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing recounts of events and experiences such as articles for a school newsletter or captions for a photo story

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a review of a song, story or film using modelled language, for example, Lagu ini tentang …; Film ini terlalu panjang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a creative text by manipulating the original text, for example, rearranging the sequence of events, adding a new element, changing the location, creating an alternative ending

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and sharing them with a real or imagined Indonesian-speaking audience using words, formulaic expressions and modelled sentences in Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating multimodal texts, such as a commercial for a new product, a short film, or a poster for an imagined event

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a procedural text, for example, a cooking show segment, instructions for making a kite

elaborations.name: VC2LIN6C05-E10 - Indonesian

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 7 and 8, Indonesian language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students use Indonesian to interact and collaborate, in person or virtually, within and beyond the classroom. They listen, speak, read, write and view to exchange information, ideas and opinions about their world. They work independently and in groups, and continue to receive feedback and support from their peers and teachers. 

Students access a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts from a variety of authentic sources, which may include audio and video clips, magazines, advertisements, images, stories and articles. They use their knowledge of metalanguage in an increasing range of contexts to reflect on similarities and differences between Indonesian, English and/or other language structures and features. They recognise that language choices reflect cultural values, beliefs and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 8, students initiate and maintain Indonesian-language interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts related to a range of interests and experiences. They use Indonesian to collaborate and problem-solve, and adjust their language in response to others. They interpret information, ideas and opinions in texts. They demonstrate understanding of the similarities and differences between languages, in both familiar and some unfamiliar contexts, by adjusting and reorganising responses. They sequence information and ideas, and select and use vocabulary, sentence structures and expressions to create texts appropriate to context, purpose and audience.

Students apply the conventions of spoken Indonesian and continue to enhance their fluency. They demonstrate understanding that spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts use different conventions, structures and features to convey meaning. They comment on structures and features of Indonesian text, using some metalanguage. They reflect on how the Indonesian language, culture and identity are interconnected, and compare this with their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E02 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E06 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U03-E03 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian has been influenced by other languages, for example, pilot (English), mie (Chinese), sepatu (Portuguese), kantor (Dutch), guru (Sanskrit), sahabat (Arabic)

elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying ‘false friends’ or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in Indonesian that can cause miscommunication

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E07 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts to entertain peers and younger audiences (e.g. a children’s story, comic, poem, short film) or participating in rehearsed and improvised role-plays based on scenarios such as meeting a celebrity, appearing on a television show or living in a past era

content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating nouns for identifying people using the base word and compound word, for example, tukang kebun; using affixations such as the -an suffix, pe- prefix and the pe- … -an construction to create nouns, for example, makanan, minuman, masakan, bacaan; pemain, pelukis, pelajaran, pekerjaan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adjectives of qualities, character and appearance when describing a character in a book or movie, for example, pintar sekali; amat menjengkelkan; sangat ramah; baik hati

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ber-, be-, me-, mem-, men-, meng- and meny- verbs to describe actions, for example, belajar; beristirahat; melihat; membeli; menulis; mengambil; menyewa

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying negation rules, for example, jangan bermain bola; tidak jauh; bukan orang Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to past and future using time indicators, for example, tadi pagi; nanti malam; sebelum; sesudah; kemudian; lalu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of question words to seek information (e.g. bagaimana; dari mana; apakah; kapan; mengapa; sudah pernah) and recognising some informal variants, for example, gimana, kenapa

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs to describe frequency, for example, jarang; sering; selalu; tidak pernah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjunctions to link and create cohesion, for example, supaya; walaupun; karena itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing appropriate classifiers to refer to the number of items or things such as fruits and classroom objects, for example, Saya mau membeli tiga buah nangka; Dia membawa sebuah buku dari perpustakaan sekolah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using yang to extend meaning and create complex sentences, for example, Ada lumba-lumba yang hidup di sungai dan ada yang hidup di laut

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct grammatical structures to make comparisons between 2 or more things, for example, paling menarik; tertinggi; sependek; Pulau Tasmania lebih besar dibandingkan dengan pulau Buton

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the object-focus construction in known and modelled contexts, for example, Bukunya dibuka; Film itu ditonton dengan keluarga

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising variations in language use such as the shortening of words and dropping the prefixes ber- and me- in informal contexts, for example, belanja; selancar; nonton; beli

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising structures indicating the level of formality in imperatives, for example, antri dong compared with harap antri
