elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying ongoing collaboration of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists and artists from Indonesia, for example, learning about batik making in central Australia, rock art in northern Australia and similar art forms in Indonesia, and developing a video or slideshow showing similarities and differences between these art forms

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and summarising information such as on the price of different products, hotel facilities, climate, or transport options, and producing a written or spoken response

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a survey to collect information from members of their class or other Indonesian speakers and presenting information to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C03-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the internet responsibly to research, or using secure digital tools to engage with youth in Indonesia or Indonesian-speaking students around the world to discover young people’s lifestyles across cultures and contexts, and comparing information from different cultural contexts to identify the influence of factors such as geography, climate, and social and community environment

elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing details from a range of texts about special occasions and ceremonies, using culture-specific terms and representations, for example, Bapak Presiden Indonesia memakai batik pada Hari Kemerdekaan Indonesia; Banyak orang Islam mudik untuk merayakan Idul Fitri

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E02 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E03 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: consolidating and using dictionary skills to locate vocabulary and improve grammatical accuracy when creating texts, for example, using the verb tables and grammar sections in a bilingual dictionary

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying language structures and cultural features that are not easily translated and/or may cause misunderstandings, and showing understanding through written, spoken or non-verbal means, for example, annotating an advertisement featuring culturally specific references to food, providing a commentary for a fashion show featuring Indonesian textiles and/or garments, demonstrating different greeting and leave-taking gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the meaning and nuances of simple Indonesian idioms and comparing with an equivalent English idiom or providing an explanation, for example, Jam karet (opposite of the Western view that ‘Time is money’); Nasi sudah menjadi bubur (‘There’s no use crying over spilt milk’)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating bilingual texts such as signs or posters to inform the school community about aspects of Indonesian culture, for example, taking off shoes when entering an Indonesian house

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting findings related to the investigation of a social or cultural issue, and summarising opinions and attitudes collected from surveys, interviews or media sources

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8C05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, sequencing information and ideas, selecting vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures appropriate to text type and context

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing and producing a text to promote an upcoming community event, an environmental issue or school activity, and initiating a call for action, for example, Selamat hari Harmoni!; Ayo hijaukan sekolah kita! Buang sampah di tempat yang benar

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a video or presentation to describe a person and/or place of significance for them (e.g. Ini rumah nenekku. Saya senang membuat kue bersama dia), or recording a short video such as a cooking demonstration, advertisement for a new product or an original rap to inform or entertain a variety of audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing simple songs, jingles, posters or advertisements for real and imaginary situations or products, for example, advertising an Australian product for the Indonesian market or vice versa

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or brochure in Indonesian for travel to their local area, including what to see and do; means of travel; best time of year to visit; what to bring and wear; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names and history

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using vocabulary and sentence structures appropriate for particular text types, for example, informative language for reports, descriptive language in documentaries, reflective language in diary or journal entries

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reporting on their own and others’ experiences of events such as school camp, a holiday or concert, joining a sports club or playing a new computer game

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing personal opinions through a review of a film, television show or new product, for example, Menurut pendapat saya; Saya pikir …; Saya suka/tidak/kurang suka …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts to entertain peers and younger audiences (e.g. a children’s story, comic, poem, short film) or participating in rehearsed and improvised role-plays based on scenarios such as meeting a celebrity, appearing on a television show or living in a past era

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating the next scene, a new character or an alternative ending for Indonesian imaginative texts such as a story, drama or film script

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an informal style of language such as the use of abbreviated forms of written words when engaging in secure digital spaces, for example, gk (tidak), plg (pulang), dgn (dengan), kmn (ke mana)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8U01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply conventions of spoken Indonesian to enhance fluency, and to respond to and create texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: stressing the penultimate syllable in multisyllabic words such as mendengarkan, melakukan, pekerjaan, perumahan, dibandingkan, kehujanan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising where to place stress in complex sentences, for example, Kami suka bermain musik bersama, tetapi kakak bermain gitar dan saya bermain angklung

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using intonation to exaggerate, emphasise a feeling or create a question, for example, Kasihan!; Wah, mahal sekali; Aduh, saya sakit perut!; Sudah makan?; Sudah makan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using authentic rhythm, intonation and pronunciation to improve fluency

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting the pitch, stress and pattern of speech according to the audience, context and purpose such as an announcement, interview, conversation or speech

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of spoken Indonesian to pronounce English loan words and assist meaning, for example, organisasi, industri, multikulturalisme

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common informal variants where appropriate in conversational settings, for example, nggak instead of tidak; kenapa instead of mengapa; lagi instead of sedang

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8U02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating nouns for identifying people using the base word and compound word, for example, tukang kebun; using affixations such as the -an suffix, pe- prefix and the pe- … -an construction to create nouns, for example, makanan, minuman, masakan, bacaan; pemain, pelukis, pelajaran, pekerjaan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adjectives of qualities, character and appearance when describing a character in a book or movie, for example, pintar sekali; amat menjengkelkan; sangat ramah; baik hati

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ber-, be-, me-, mem-, men-, meng- and meny- verbs to describe actions, for example, belajar; beristirahat; melihat; membeli; menulis; mengambil; menyewa

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying negation rules, for example, jangan bermain bola; tidak jauh; bukan orang Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to past and future using time indicators, for example, tadi pagi; nanti malam; sebelum; sesudah; kemudian; lalu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of question words to seek information (e.g. bagaimana; dari mana; apakah; kapan; mengapa; sudah pernah) and recognising some informal variants, for example, gimana, kenapa

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs to describe frequency, for example, jarang; sering; selalu; tidak pernah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjunctions to link and create cohesion, for example, supaya; walaupun; karena itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing appropriate classifiers to refer to the number of items or things such as fruits and classroom objects, for example, Saya mau membeli tiga buah nangka; Dia membawa sebuah buku dari perpustakaan sekolah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using yang to extend meaning and create complex sentences, for example, Ada lumba-lumba yang hidup di sungai dan ada yang hidup di laut

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct grammatical structures to make comparisons between 2 or more things, for example, paling menarik; tertinggi; sependek; Pulau Tasmania lebih besar dibandingkan dengan pulau Buton

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the object-focus construction in known and modelled contexts, for example, Bukunya dibuka; Film itu ditonton dengan keluarga

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising variations in language use such as the shortening of words and dropping the prefixes ber- and me- in informal contexts, for example, belanja; selancar; nonton; beli

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising structures indicating the level of formality in imperatives, for example, antri dong compared with harap antri

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8U03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on the structures and features of Indonesian, and compare them with English and/or other languages, using some metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian uses classifiers such as kota, pulau and pantai to categorise a place

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing language features such as word order, base words and affixations, using relevant metalanguage such as verbs, adjectives, nouns and pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the forms, features and purpose of texts in Indonesian and other languages such as how texts are organised in terms of layout, sequencing of ideas, headings and stylistic devices

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian has been influenced by other languages, for example, pilot (English), mie (Chinese), sepatu (Portuguese), kantor (Dutch), guru (Sanskrit), sahabat (Arabic)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U04-E04 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: appreciating that elements of Indonesian culture are reflected through behaviour and attitudes such as halus, sombong and sopan santun

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining how cultural expectations vary across Indonesia, for example, Kami makan babi guling di rumah Made; Saya mau sholat dulu; Permisi, ya, Mas …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing traditional methods that Indonesian speakers use to preserve language and culture; comparing these with examples of cultural artefacts such as dance, songs, artwork, artefacts or traditions, from a range of different cultures; and identifying how they strengthen connections to values and identity, for example, discussing the significance of a possum-skin coat for some Aboriginal Peoples and sharing similarities and differences between cultural artefacts in other languages and cultures represented in the classroom

substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts related to their experiences, feelings and views, adjusting their language in response to others

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging opinions with a partner about family, friends, teachers, subjects, entertainment, sport and leisure, for example, Saya pikir Matematika menarik sekali. Kalau kamu, bagaimana? and using Indonesian fillers such as anu … and exclamations Aduh! Oh begitu! in these interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing, comparing and clarifying aspects of their personal worlds such as school or home life (e.g. Tugas saya memberi makan anjing; Setiap hari kami sholat) and recounting and sharing information related to significant events, special occasions and milestones during class discussions or activities, for example, Tahun lalu saya pergi ke Bali dengan keluarga saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and expressing preferences and feelings with students from a real or imagined Indonesian-speaking class, using secure digital resources (including interactive multimedia) to discuss significant issues related to the local community and environment, for example, Saya lebih suka berenang di pantai daripada kolam renang di kota karena lebih bersih. Kamu melakukan apa pada hari Clean Up Australia?

elaborations.elaboration_text: socialising in simulated scenarios with friends and family at events, for example, Kamu bersekolah di mana?; Suka bermain olahraga?; Bisa datang ke pesta ulang tahun saya?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with peers using various media to ask and respond to questions, for example, email exchanges with students at a sister school in Indonesia or with students learning Indonesian elsewhere in Australia

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 9 and 10, Indonesian language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students use Indonesian to initiate and sustain interactions that communicate their own and others’ experiences of the world. They listen, speak, read, write and view to communicate with speakers of Indonesian locally and globally through authentic community and moderated, secure online events. They access and create spoken and written texts, increasingly of their own choosing. They continue to receive guidance, feedback and support from their peers and teachers. 

Students access an increasing range of authentic and purpose-developed resources, which may include textbooks, audio and video clips, feature articles, television programs, teacher-moderated social media and other multimodal texts. They expand their knowledge of spoken and written Indonesian language structures and features. They acknowledge that there are diverse influences on ways of communication and cultural identity, and that these influences can shape their own behaviours, values and beliefs.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 10, students contribute to and extend interactions in Indonesian in increasingly unfamiliar contexts related to a wide range of interests and issues. They interpret texts by identifying and evaluating information, ideas and perspectives. They show understanding of how features of language can be used to influence audience response. They create texts, selecting and manipulating language for a range of contexts, purposes and audiences. They apply and use complex sentences and structures to create and respond to spoken and written texts. They use a variety of tenses to sequence events and use language structures and features to enhance meaning and cohesion.

Students incorporate the features and conventions of spoken Indonesian to enhance and extend fluency. They demonstrate understanding of the conventions of spoken and written texts, in both formal and informal contexts, and the connections between them. They apply knowledge of language structures and features to make and predict meaning. They analyse Indonesian texts using metalanguage. They reflect on their own cultural perspectives and identity, and draw on their experience of learning Indonesian to evaluate how this learning influences their ideas and ways of communicating.

elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in exchanges, using strategies to initiate and sustain interactions and conversations (e.g. Boleh saya bertanya …?; Permisi tanya, Pak/Bu?; Apa maksudmu?; Maaf?; Oh, begitu …), by playing a conversation game where students try to extend a conversation for as long as possible using these interactions

elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in oral and written texts to accept or refuse invitations, make excuses and apologise by participating in role-plays to plan weekend events and activities, for example, Terima kasih banyak, saya mau ikut acara; Jam berapa filmnya mulai?; Maaf lain kali ya saya ada acara lain; Mohon maaf saya tidak bisa hadir karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging cards or messages to express feelings or attitudes, such as expressing regret, sympathy, gratitude or congratulations, for example, Kami turut berduka cita; Selamat atas kemenangan lomba pidato bahasa Indonesia!; Kami mengucapkan banyak terima kasih atas waktu dan bantuan Bapak/Ibu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving encouragement, criticism or praise to peers during games, debates or events, for example, Saya setuju; Memang; Mungkin sedikit terlalu …; Ide bagus; Rapi sekali!; Keren!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with peers using secure digital technology to build relationships (e.g. talking about school life and part-time work), for example, Jam berapa kelas mulai di sekolahmu?; Saya punya pekerjaan sambilan/paruh waktu di toko kecil dan pada masa depan mau membeli mobil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with an audience after a speech or presentation to clarify or extend meaning with questions related to topics such as the environment, teenage aspirations or pop culture, adjusting language used according to the specified audience

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in improvisations and scenario activities such as drama games to encourage sustained spontaneous interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising for making mistakes or misunderstanding in interactions, for example, Boleh saya serahkan tugas pada hari Senin?; Mohon maaf saya kurang tahu; Wah, saya pikir saya bisa menyelesaikan tugas ini minggu depan. Maaf sekali!

content_descriptions.text: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in class discussions using language to seek and express opinions by discussing issues important to members of the class such as school rules, environmental challenges or social media, for example, dibandingkan, di satu pihak … di lain pihak; Saya tidak heran karena …; Tidak mengherankan bahwa …; Penting sekali untuk … Setuju, nggak?; Bagaimana pendapat kamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in simulated online forums to raise awareness of and discuss environmental, social or ethical issues

elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating arrangements, weighing up alternatives and reaching shared decisions by participating in a role-play where students plan weekend activities/events or plan holidays, for example, Sudah ada acara besok malam?; Sudah ada rencana untuk akhir minggu ini?; Bagaimana kalau kita ke …; Lebih baik naik … atau …?; Kamu pilih yang mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing ideas and suggesting options to solve problems, for example, Menurut pendapat saya …; Sebaiknya …; Mungkin lebih baik kalau …; Sesudah dipikirkan dengan serius …; Kesimpulannya …; Kesimpulan saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using persuasive language to encourage a change of opinion such as writing an essay or creating a targeted advertisement, for example, Harganya sama sekali tidak mahal!; Merk ini mempunyai kualitas tinggi!; Sebaiknya, anak-anak Australia memilih untuk belajar Bahasa Indonesia sebagai pilihan pelajaran bahasa asing; Tidak dapat disangkabahwa …; Seperti yang sudah kita ketahui, bahwa …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating a particular course of action, for example, planning a day out with a guest; creating an itinerary for a group of Indonesian visitors; choosing Independence Day games for the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a class blog, reflecting on and sharing experiences about topics of interest

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving advice to a friend regarding a personal choice, for example, Sebaiknya …; Seharusnya …; Mesti dipikirkan akibatnya bahwa …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a news clip or part of an informative video and using what was introduced in the clip as a prompt for discussion, starting with summarising, and then providing their own opinion and justifying this opinion

as_extracts.name: LINDF1010-E02
as_extracts.description: They interpret texts by identifying and evaluating information, ideas and perspectives.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: interpret and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching a topic of personal interest, concept or issue drawn from another learning area, to write an essay, report or develop a multimodal presentation

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information to evaluate and debate issues of interest such as the environment, expectations of teenagers and cultural practices (e.g. rites of passage), using persuasive or evaluative language, for example, Saya percaya …; Ini pasti berguna bagi …; Mau tidak mau …; Salah satu keuntungannya adalah …; Aspek positifnya termasuk …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating current Indonesian video or blog sites relating to current affairs, fashion, popular culture and music artists, to review and analyse information and use of language for a specified purpose and audience, such as a podcast or newspaper article

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing texts such as interviews, documentaries and speeches to obtain a new perspective, and using the information to demonstrate understanding, for example, Kata Presiden Indonesia, keadaan …; Yang sudah dilaporkan …; Seperti yang sudah disebut oleh …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a range of texts such as music videos, short films and movies to review and express personal opinions about key aspects by writing a review or a personal reflection for a simulated online forum or blog, for example, Pada pendapat saya cerita ini …; Saya kurang suka jenis film fantasi karena …; Tokoh utamanya menarik sekali karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: summarising the key points from a range of texts such as teacher-curated blog posts and interviews

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing artwork from a local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander artist, and then writing a script of a speech to present to a group of Indonesian speakers introducing the artist

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching information about a significant Indonesian person or character and demonstrating understanding by creating an imagined interview with the person or a diary entry written from the research subject’s point of view

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a variety of texts to understand the experiences of Indonesian-speaking youth in daily life activities, and collating information to share on a teacher-moderated blog or online platform titled ‘A day in the life of an Indonesian high school student’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining graphs, a table of statistics or pictures, and using the information gained from the texts to respond orally or in written form, for example, writing a formal letter to a member of parliament, requesting change based on evidence from the texts

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between fact and opinion in texts such as articles and reports, and using critical literacy skills to recognise bias such as identifying the audience and purpose of the text, for example, Itu berita palsu; Kami tahu bahwa informasi itu bukan fakta karena …; Kita tidak boleh cepat percaya pada …; Berita tersebut harus diuji kebenarannya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the use of non-verbal and spoken language to communicate nuanced cultural meaning such as gestures used to accompany expressions of interaction, for example, Tambah lagi …; Minta maaf kalau ada yang salah; Kalau tidak salah …; Saya minta maaf kalau ada hal-hal yang tidak sengaja saya lakukan …; Mohon maaf kalau ada kata-kata yang menyinggung perasaan …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and responding to key messages, values and characteristics in traditional texts such as dongeng, wayang, short stories and poetry, and conveying their meaning and actions for modern interpretations, for example, tokoh Semar, Si Kancil stories, legends such as Malin Kundang, Tangkuban Perahu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and explaining the use of images, sounds, gestures and language choices to convey cultural concepts and ideals in Indonesian texts, for example, signs, dial tones, anjing menggonggong

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing excerpts from interviews with public figures (e.g. sports stars, musicians, actors), noting how vocabulary, phrases or gestures are used to emphasise or clarify key information, and collating a list of new phrases and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different resources for interpretation and translation by discussing, comparing, back-translating and checking contextual understanding of individual translations

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with translations of Indonesian expressions or idioms, for example, Terlepas dari mulut buaya, masuk ke mulut harimau; Biar lambat asal selamat

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating expressions used in Australian English for Indonesian speakers (e.g. ‘bush tucker’, ‘she’ll be right’, ‘schoolies’), and identifying Indonesian words or phrases that may be difficult to translate into English

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting textual conventions popular with young Indonesian speakers, such as contractions, abbreviations and acronyms used in text messaging, for example, writing and responding to a series of text messages using acronyms such as wkwkwk = laughter, dgn = dengan, and Gpp = Gak Apa-apa

content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate Indonesian texts, using metalanguage to analyse language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying language structures and features using metalanguage in Indonesian and English, for example, kata dasar (base word), kata kerja (verb), bentuk pasif (passive form), akronim (acronym), singkatan (abbreviation) and creating a table of relevant language for a personal dictionary

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing language and techniques used in contemporary drama, television programs, poetry and film such as hyperbole, imagery, humour, music and camera angles

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that variations to standard Indonesian spelling of loan words such as bis/bus, sistim/sistem, propinsi/provinsi, moderen/modern, are the product of language evolution and comparing it with similar evolution in English and other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and applying formatting conventions in Indonesian texts such as an academic report, essay, article, email or text message

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing linguistic structures and features in spoken and written texts such as media, television, advertisements, face-to-face conversations and emails

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the variety of spoken and written colloquial forms, for example, bahasa gaul, bahasa SMS, and using a Venn diagram to compare with similar forms in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the language of requests and prohibitions in different contexts, for example, mohon; harap; tolong; jangan; dilarang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the language of social and political messages that have been used to express attitudes, beliefs and values at different times throughout history, for example, Mohon tidak merokok; Jauhi narkoba; persatuan dan kesatuan bangsa Indonesia; anak bangsa; Dua anak cukup

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E05 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: using conventions of Indonesian speech structure in formal situations, for example, Salam sejahtera bagi kita semua …; Terima kasih atas …; Mohon maaf kalau ada kata-kata yang kurang berkenan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E07 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: applying appropriate pauses and pace of delivery to convey meaning, emphasis, feelings and emotion, and to create effects in spoken texts, for example, recording themselves presenting a speech or participating in a conversation, and reflecting on how they could improve or adjust the delivery of the information

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E05 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E01 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E02 - Indonesian

Kenapa/Mengapa Anda lebih suka anjing daripada kucing?

elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in oral and written texts to accept or refuse invitations, make excuses and apologise by participating in role-plays to plan weekend events and activities, for example, Terima kasih banyak, saya mau ikut acara; Jam berapa filmnya mulai?; Maaf lain kali ya saya ada acara lain; Mohon maaf saya tidak bisa hadir karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging cards or messages to express feelings or attitudes, such as expressing regret, sympathy, gratitude or congratulations, for example, Kami turut berduka cita; Selamat atas kemenangan lomba pidato bahasa Indonesia!; Kami mengucapkan banyak terima kasih atas waktu dan bantuan Bapak/Ibu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving encouragement, criticism or praise to peers during games, debates or events, for example, Saya setuju; Memang; Mungkin sedikit terlalu …; Ide bagus; Rapi sekali!; Keren!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with peers using secure digital technology to build relationships (e.g. talking about school life and part-time work), for example, Jam berapa kelas mulai di sekolahmu?; Saya punya pekerjaan sambilan/paruh waktu di toko kecil dan pada masa depan mau membeli mobil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with an audience after a speech or presentation to clarify or extend meaning with questions related to topics such as the environment, teenage aspirations or pop culture, adjusting language used according to the specified audience

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in improvisations and scenario activities such as drama games to encourage sustained spontaneous interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising for making mistakes or misunderstanding in interactions, for example, Boleh saya serahkan tugas pada hari Senin?; Mohon maaf saya kurang tahu; Wah, saya pikir saya bisa menyelesaikan tugas ini minggu depan. Maaf sekali!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing ideas and suggesting options to solve problems, for example, Menurut pendapat saya …; Sebaiknya …; Mungkin lebih baik kalau …; Sesudah dipikirkan dengan serius …; Kesimpulannya …; Kesimpulan saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E05 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E06 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a class blog, reflecting on and sharing experiences about topics of interest

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving advice to a friend regarding a personal choice, for example, Sebaiknya …; Seharusnya …; Mesti dipikirkan akibatnya bahwa …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E04 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E06 - Indonesian

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C04 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between fact and opinion in texts such as articles and reports, and using critical literacy skills to recognise bias such as identifying the audience and purpose of the text, for example, Itu berita palsu; Kami tahu bahwa informasi itu bukan fakta karena …; Kita tidak boleh cepat percaya pada …; Berita tersebut harus diuji kebenarannya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the use of non-verbal and spoken language to communicate nuanced cultural meaning such as gestures used to accompany expressions of interaction, for example, Tambah lagi …; Minta maaf kalau ada yang salah; Kalau tidak salah …; Saya minta maaf kalau ada hal-hal yang tidak sengaja saya lakukan …; Mohon maaf kalau ada kata-kata yang menyinggung perasaan …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and responding to key messages, values and characteristics in traditional texts such as dongeng, wayang, short stories and poetry, and conveying their meaning and actions for modern interpretations, for example, tokoh Semar, Si Kancil stories, legends such as Malin Kundang, Tangkuban Perahu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and explaining the use of images, sounds, gestures and language choices to convey cultural concepts and ideals in Indonesian texts, for example, signs, dial tones, anjing menggonggong

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing excerpts from interviews with public figures (e.g. sports stars, musicians, actors), noting how vocabulary, phrases or gestures are used to emphasise or clarify key information, and collating a list of new phrases and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E06 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with translations of Indonesian expressions or idioms, for example, Terlepas dari mulut buaya, masuk ke mulut harimau; Biar lambat asal selamat

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating expressions used in Australian English for Indonesian speakers (e.g. ‘bush tucker’, ‘she’ll be right’, ‘schoolies’), and identifying Indonesian words or phrases that may be difficult to translate into English

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E09 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the variety of spoken and written colloquial forms, for example, bahasa gaul, bahasa SMS, and using a Venn diagram to compare with similar forms in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the language of requests and prohibitions in different contexts, for example, mohon; harap; tolong; jangan; dilarang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the language of social and political messages that have been used to express attitudes, beliefs and values at different times throughout history, for example, Mohon tidak merokok; Jauhi narkoba; persatuan dan kesatuan bangsa Indonesia; anak bangsa; Dua anak cukup

as_extracts.name: LINDF1010-E11
as_extracts.description: They reflect on their own cultural perspectives and identity, and draw on their experience of learning Indonesian to evaluate how this learning influences their ideas and ways of communicating.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10U04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and evaluating ways in which texts such as films, plays and songs convey social issues and values

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that many Indonesians may be bilingual or multilingual and can move between these languages depending on the context

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how language variation can reflect cultural and social identity, inclusion or exclusion, for example, reading speeches or advertisements and analysing the language used, identifying persuasive devices such as inclusive or emotive language

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how jargon or specific terms may be used to express membership and identity such as within the religious groups, for example, Insya’allah; Puji Tuhan; Syukur; Alhamdulilah; Om swastiastu; sesajen

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and discussing how the linguistic diversity of Indonesia reveals cultural diversity, and recognising how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or reading examples of an Acknowledgement of Country in Indonesian, and creating their own version that names the local Country for an Indonesian-speaking audience

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how the Indonesian language may reflect cultural perspectives such as collectivism, harmony, belief in fate and humility (e.g. setahu saya, kalau saya tidak salah, numpang tanya, permisi dulu) and the use of kami (meaning ‘we’ or ‘us’, such as in Hormat kami; Kami mohon maaf yang sebesar-besarnya atas …; Belum bertemu jodoh)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering the cultural significance of experiences and events that shape identity such as potong gigi, sweet 17th birthdays and graduation, and how this is reflected in language, for example, how young people may introduce themselves (Saya sudah tamat sekolah; Dia sudah akil baligh)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the influence of activists, artists, and authors on language, art and ways of thinking and how they may influence attitudes and values regarding social issues, for example, the artwork of Eko Nugroho; the writing of Pramoedya Ananta Toer and Kartini; the use of Kak in some activist contexts as a gender-neutral alternative to Ibu and Bapak

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts related to their own and others’ experiences of the world, adjusting their language in response to others

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and sustaining conversation by introducing topics, inviting contributions or asking for clarification

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending interaction by seeking opinion and agreement, comparing and contrasting likes and interests by surveying members of the class to create a profile of student interests or interviewing members of the class to find someone with similar interests, for example, Penyanyi pop favoritmu siapa? Kenapa/Mengapa Anda lebih suka anjing daripada kucing?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in exchanges, using strategies to initiate and sustain interactions and conversations (e.g. Boleh saya bertanya …?; Permisi tanya, Pak/Bu?; Apa maksudmu?; Maaf?; Oh, begitu …), by playing a conversation game where students try to extend a conversation for as long as possible using these interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in oral and written texts to accept or refuse invitations, make excuses and apologise by participating in role-plays to plan weekend events and activities, for example, Terima kasih banyak, saya mau ikut acara; Jam berapa filmnya mulai?; Maaf lain kali ya saya ada acara lain; Mohon maaf saya tidak bisa hadir karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging cards or messages to express feelings or attitudes, such as expressing regret, sympathy, gratitude or congratulations, for example, Kami turut berduka cita; Selamat atas kemenangan lomba pidato bahasa Indonesia!; Kami mengucapkan banyak terima kasih atas waktu dan bantuan Bapak/Ibu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving encouragement, criticism or praise to peers during games, debates or events, for example, Saya setuju; Memang; Mungkin sedikit terlalu …; Ide bagus; Rapi sekali!; Keren!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with peers using secure digital technology to build relationships (e.g. talking about school life and part-time work), for example, Jam berapa kelas mulai di sekolahmu?; Saya punya pekerjaan sambilan/paruh waktu di toko kecil dan pada masa depan mau membeli mobil

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with an audience after a speech or presentation to clarify or extend meaning with questions related to topics such as the environment, teenage aspirations or pop culture, adjusting language used according to the specified audience

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in improvisations and scenario activities such as drama games to encourage sustained spontaneous interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C01-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising for making mistakes or misunderstanding in interactions, for example, Boleh saya serahkan tugas pada hari Senin?; Mohon maaf saya kurang tahu; Wah, saya pikir saya bisa menyelesaikan tugas ini minggu depan. Maaf sekali!

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in class discussions using language to seek and express opinions by discussing issues important to members of the class such as school rules, environmental challenges or social media, for example, dibandingkan, di satu pihak … di lain pihak; Saya tidak heran karena …; Tidak mengherankan bahwa …; Penting sekali untuk … Setuju, nggak?; Bagaimana pendapat kamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in simulated online forums to raise awareness of and discuss environmental, social or ethical issues

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS3
organising_ideas.text: Economic, social, environmental and cultural systems influence the sustainability of Earth’s systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating arrangements, weighing up alternatives and reaching shared decisions by participating in a role-play where students plan weekend activities/events or plan holidays, for example, Sudah ada acara besok malam?; Sudah ada rencana untuk akhir minggu ini?; Bagaimana kalau kita ke …; Lebih baik naik … atau …?; Kamu pilih yang mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing ideas and suggesting options to solve problems, for example, Menurut pendapat saya …; Sebaiknya …; Mungkin lebih baik kalau …; Sesudah dipikirkan dengan serius …; Kesimpulannya …; Kesimpulan saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using persuasive language to encourage a change of opinion such as writing an essay or creating a targeted advertisement, for example, Harganya sama sekali tidak mahal!; Merk ini mempunyai kualitas tinggi!; Sebaiknya, anak-anak Australia memilih untuk belajar Bahasa Indonesia sebagai pilihan pelajaran bahasa asing; Tidak dapat disangkabahwa …; Seperti yang sudah kita ketahui, bahwa …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating a particular course of action, for example, planning a day out with a guest; creating an itinerary for a group of Indonesian visitors; choosing Independence Day games for the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a class blog, reflecting on and sharing experiences about topics of interest

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving advice to a friend regarding a personal choice, for example, Sebaiknya …; Seharusnya …; Mesti dipikirkan akibatnya bahwa …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a news clip or part of an informative video and using what was introduced in the clip as a prompt for discussion, starting with summarising, and then providing their own opinion and justifying this opinion

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpret and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to context, purpose and audience
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching a topic of personal interest, concept or issue drawn from another learning area, to write an essay, report or develop a multimodal presentation

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information to evaluate and debate issues of interest such as the environment, expectations of teenagers and cultural practices (e.g. rites of passage), using persuasive or evaluative language, for example, Saya percaya …; Ini pasti berguna bagi …; Mau tidak mau …; Salah satu keuntungannya adalah …; Aspek positifnya termasuk …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating current Indonesian video or blog sites relating to current affairs, fashion, popular culture and music artists, to review and analyse information and use of language for a specified purpose and audience, such as a podcast or newspaper article

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing texts such as interviews, documentaries and speeches to obtain a new perspective, and using the information to demonstrate understanding, for example, Kata Presiden Indonesia, keadaan …; Yang sudah dilaporkan …; Seperti yang sudah disebut oleh …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a range of texts such as music videos, short films and movies to review and express personal opinions about key aspects by writing a review or a personal reflection for a simulated online forum or blog, for example, Pada pendapat saya cerita ini …; Saya kurang suka jenis film fantasi karena …; Tokoh utamanya menarik sekali karena …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: summarising the key points from a range of texts such as teacher-curated blog posts and interviews

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing artwork from a local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander artist, and then writing a script of a speech to present to a group of Indonesian speakers introducing the artist

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching information about a significant Indonesian person or character and demonstrating understanding by creating an imagined interview with the person or a diary entry written from the research subject’s point of view

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a variety of texts to understand the experiences of Indonesian-speaking youth in daily life activities, and collating information to share on a teacher-moderated blog or online platform titled ‘A day in the life of an Indonesian high school student’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C03-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining graphs, a table of statistics or pictures, and using the information gained from the texts to respond orally or in written form, for example, writing a formal letter to a member of parliament, requesting change based on evidence from the texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C04 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between fact and opinion in texts such as articles and reports, and using critical literacy skills to recognise bias such as identifying the audience and purpose of the text, for example, Itu berita palsu; Kami tahu bahwa informasi itu bukan fakta karena …; Kita tidak boleh cepat percaya pada …; Berita tersebut harus diuji kebenarannya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating the use of non-verbal and spoken language to communicate nuanced cultural meaning such as gestures used to accompany expressions of interaction, for example, Tambah lagi …; Minta maaf kalau ada yang salah; Kalau tidak salah …; Saya minta maaf kalau ada hal-hal yang tidak sengaja saya lakukan …; Mohon maaf kalau ada kata-kata yang menyinggung perasaan …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and responding to key messages, values and characteristics in traditional texts such as dongeng, wayang, short stories and poetry, and conveying their meaning and actions for modern interpretations, for example, tokoh Semar, Si Kancil stories, legends such as Malin Kundang, Tangkuban Perahu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and explaining the use of images, sounds, gestures and language choices to convey cultural concepts and ideals in Indonesian texts, for example, signs, dial tones, anjing menggonggong

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing excerpts from interviews with public figures (e.g. sports stars, musicians, actors), noting how vocabulary, phrases or gestures are used to emphasise or clarify key information, and collating a list of new phrases and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different resources for interpretation and translation by discussing, comparing, back-translating and checking contextual understanding of individual translations

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with translations of Indonesian expressions or idioms, for example, Terlepas dari mulut buaya, masuk ke mulut harimau; Biar lambat asal selamat

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating expressions used in Australian English for Indonesian speakers (e.g. ‘bush tucker’, ‘she’ll be right’, ‘schoolies’), and identifying Indonesian words or phrases that may be difficult to translate into English

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting textual conventions popular with young Indonesian speakers, such as contractions, abbreviations and acronyms used in text messaging, for example, writing and responding to a series of text messages using acronyms such as wkwkwk = laughter, dgn = dengan, and Gpp = Gak Apa-apa

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10C05 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of textual conventions to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an informative multimodal presentation such as an infographic or webpage, comparing different perspectives on the same event or issue, for example, different approaches to key personal milestones such as coming of age or weddings

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: documenting trends in popular culture such as food, fashion or music; or profiling a unique place, practise or event, for example, kampung pelangi; budidaya rumput laut; hari Kartini

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: debating topics such as part-time work, balancing study and leisure, or changing the school uniform, using appropriate expressions to explain and justify opinions, for example, alasannya begini; ternyata; tidak dapat disangka; mau tak mau; sehingga; setidak-tidaknya; jangan-jangan; oleh karena itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a text such as a blog or an essay to persuade an audience to take action on a particular issue, for example, recycling; participation in sport; supporting a local cause using language appropriate to the audience

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or reading Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ stories in English, and adapting them to share with an Indonesian-speaking audience, considering words and concepts that are not easily translated and ways to use visuals to aid understanding

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or a contribution for a school newsletter in Indonesian, reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing an alternative ending to an imaginative text, introducing a new character, changing the setting or adding a major event

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: rewriting texts such as fairytales, legends or myths from a different perspective

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reviewing a video clip, short film or film to describe and evaluate the story or elements

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10C05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing persuasive multimodal texts, for example, advertisements, announcements or reviews

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10U01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken Indonesian to extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and applying the role of stress and rhythm in creating emphasis, for example, recurring patterns, rhymes and onomatopoeia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using tone to communicate meaning and intention, for example, kasihan deh, ikut dong

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: dropping affixation and using base words to convey meaning in informal conversations, for example, Mau main nggak?; Dah nonton, belum?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: knowing when to pause in complex sentences with embedded clauses

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the correct pronunciation of words with complex affixations, for example, dipengaruhi, sebesar-besarnya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conventions of Indonesian speech structure in formal situations, for example, Salam sejahtera bagi kita semua …; Terima kasih atas …; Mohon maaf kalau ada kata-kata yang kurang berkenan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing discussion points in an argument by using sentence starters and connectors, for example, Pertama- tama … ; Harap maklum …; Lebih lagi …; Namun …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying appropriate pauses and pace of delivery to convey meaning, emphasis, feelings and emotion, and to create effects in spoken texts, for example, recording themselves presenting a speech or participating in a conversation, and reflecting on how they could improve or adjust the delivery of the information

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10U02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to predict meaning, and to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using compound nouns (e.g. sayur-mayur, merah darah), comparing them with English compound nouns and discussing differences in word order and meaning development

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to groups with plural classifiers and pronouns, for example, kaum, para, sekalian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying appropriate terms of address such as kak, dik, Mbak, Bang, Neng and particles such as diminutive Si and honorific Sang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prior knowledge of common and proper nouns to match meaning of acronyms, for example, puskesmas, PenJas, Sulut, Kaltim, Presdir

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: predicting meaning of abbreviations appropriately, for example, Saya bersekolah di SMA Melton; Maaf, aku lupa bawa HP-ku!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the relevant classifier to refer to number of items, for example, Saya bermaksud membeli dua sisir pisang tetapi di pasar pisang sudah habis; Bung Karno pernah tinggal di sebuah kampung dekat kota Surabaya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using affixation to create texts with complex or abstract ideas, for example, pelajaran, pertandingan, kesehatan, kedatangan, kecantikan, kehutanan, perekonomian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10U02-E08 - Indonesian

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 7 and 8, students are beginning their learning of Indonesian language, and this will be influenced by their prior experiences of language learning. Students use Indonesian to describe their personal worlds and to interact and collaborate with their teachers and peers within and beyond the classroom. Listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing activities are supported by scaffolding, modelling and feedback. 

Students access authentic and purpose-developed spoken, written, viewed and multimodal resources, which may include conversations, audio and video clips, textbooks, advertisements, images, teacher-curated content from blogs, and magazines. They use their knowledge of metalanguage to reflect on similarities and differences in language structures and features between Indonesian, English and/or other languages. They recognise that language choices reflect cultural values, beliefs and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 8, students use Indonesian to interact and collaborate with others, and to share information and plan activities in familiar contexts. They recognise and respond to familiar gestures, questions and instructions when interacting with others. They locate and respond to information in texts and use visual and contextual cues to help make meaning. They respond in Indonesian or English, and demonstrate their understanding of context, purpose and audience in texts. They use familiar language, modelled sentences and grammatical structures to create texts appropriate to audience.

Students begin to use pronunciation, intonation and rhythm in spoken Indonesian to develop fluency. They demonstrate understanding that Indonesian has conventions for non-verbal, spoken and written communication. They comment on aspects of Indonesian and English language structures and features, using some metalanguage. They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.
