elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing texts (e.g. signs, advertisements or artworks) and extracting information to answer questions or create short texts such as captions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, classifying and summarising information such as results of class surveys (e.g. 30% murid suka berolahraga air, 40% suka berlibur di gunung) and using questions, for example, Kamu suka makan apa?; Kamu suka pergi ke mana pada akhir minggu?; Apa binatang favoritmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching and comparing different types of eating venues in Indonesia such as rumah makan Padang, warung, kaki lima, restoran to make menu selections, for example, Mau mencoba makanan apa? Mau mencoba minuman apa? Sudah makan rendang?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing cartoons, comics and stories, and expressing opinions and ideas, for example, Saya suka / kurang suka; Saya rasa / pikir; Pada pendapat saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching information to develop an itinerary for an imagined holiday using modelled vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, for example, Berangkat dari Jakarta jam 08:00; Sampai di Makassar jam 11:00; Pada hari Senin ikut tur ke obyek wisata Rammang-Rammang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: navigating secure online applications to find out about transport and services in Indonesia, using information in a simulated conversation with a taxi driver or person in a hotel, for example, Berapa tarif dua malam di hotel?; Bagaimana fasilitas kamar/hotel?; Apakah termasuk makan pagi?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a film or video and writing a summary of the plot or a profile of a character, Saya suka ceritanya karena dramatis; Bayu tinggal di Jakarta dan dia suka bermain sepak bola

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching a topic of interest in Indonesian and presenting information using modelled vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions, for example, creating an infographic; writing a short report for the school newsletter; creating a digital presentation for the class

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to Indonesian texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in Indonesian in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using skills that promote reading for understanding by, for example, identifying all the words they understand in an Indonesian sentence or words that are similar in Indonesian and English, to help make an ‘educated guess’ about the meaning of the sentence

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing strategies to interpret body language and non-verbal cues, for example, senam and teacher gestures and creating and performing a short comedy skit demonstrating miscommunications

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled texts such as cloze passages or songs in dictation exercises to develop listening for understanding

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting Indonesian gestures to convey meaning and using them appropriately in classroom interactions with peers and teachers, for example, only using the right hand to pass objects, using the thumb to point

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dictionaries or online translation tools to find meaning of words or expressions and using context to assist understanding, for example, using context to determine whether halus is referring to refined behaviour, smooth texture or a well-crafted object

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of a text, including versions created by online translators, and discussing any issues that emerge

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prior knowledge to access culture-specific vocabulary and images to interpret meaning, for example, using a music video to understand song lyrics

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring, expanding and consolidating word usage using online translation tools to interpret idioms, proverbs, sayings and set phrases, for example, Jam karet; Sedia payung sebelum hujan; Rajin pangkal pandai, hemat pangkal kaya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print and online dictionaries, selecting appropriate meaning from alternatives provided and comparing translations with peers, explaining cultural references and expressions and any aspects ‘lost in translation’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying ‘false friends’ or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in Indonesian that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken Indonesian to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the sound of Indonesian is represented using the Roman alphabet

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the Indonesian alphabet to spell out names or expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the pronunciation of the Indonesian alphabet modelled by the teacher or audio scripts and participating in activities such as spelling words out loud, games using letter patterns or hotel check-in scenarios, for example, d-e-w-i

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating modelled phrases and sentences using Indonesian rhythm and intonation, for example, Terima kasih; Saya membaca buku; Saya naik becak ke sekolah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the distinctive sounds and sound combinations of Indonesian (e.g. namanya, mau, baik, umur, tinggal, membaca) by listening to short audio or video texts and tracking how many sound combinations they can hear

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising intonation for questions (with or without question words), statements, commands and interjections (e.g. Wah!; Aduh!; Oh begitu!; Sudah makan?; Sudah makan) by listening to audio and video clips for the target phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading out loud to develop correct pronunciation, intonation, rhythm and stress by participating in reading games and races

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some informal variants and understanding the appropriate settings for their use, such as makasih instead of terima kasih, and participating in short skits where the language is used in both correct and incorrect contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning sentences (e.g. identifying and describing mystery objects as they are lifted out of a box) using the demonstratives ini/itu, for example, Ini buku saya; Itu temannya

as_extracts.name: LIND7108-E04
as_extracts.description: They respond in Indonesian or English, and demonstrate their understanding of context, purpose and audience in texts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using subject+verb+object modelled sentence structures (e.g. Saya belajar bahasa Indonesia) and using correct word order noun+adjectives to describe qualities of nouns such as people, objects and places, for example, komputer baru, sepatu bagus, anjing besar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct word order for possessive pronouns such as saya/aku/ku, Anda/kamu/mu, dia/nya, mereka, for example, nama saya …; pena dia …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing qualities, for example, lebih … daripada

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using interrogatives playing a game of 20 questions, for example, siapa; apa; bagaimana; berapa; dari mana; di mana; ke mana; apakah; kapan; jam berapa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negating using tidak, bukan and belum, for example, Sudah siap? Belum; Saya tidak punya buku; Mereka bukan teman saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cardinal numbers to count (e.g. puluh, belas, ratus, ribu, juta); using ordinal numbers to sequence order, for example, pertama, ke+number

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating quantity using plurals, for example, tiga buku; banyak buku; buku-buku

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking ideas using conjunctions, for example, dan, karena, tetapi, atau, dengan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using imperatives, for example, Bacalah!; Tulislah!; Dengarkanlah!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing simple actions using base words, for example, makan; minum; pulang; pergi; suka; tidur; noticing ber- and me- verbs

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to existence/presence/possession, for example, ada, tidak ada; Ibu ada kelas; Dia punya bola; Ada dua lapangan bola basket di sekolah tetapi tidak ada kolam renang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to give directions and information about location, for example, di/ke, dari, di sini, di sana, di atas, di bawah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to the present, past and future using time indicators such as hari ini; sekarang; kemarin; sebelum; sesudah; besok

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing modality, for example, bisa; harus; boleh; mau

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using duplication to indicate extended or repeated action, for example, berjalan-jalan; bermalas-malas; duduk-duduk; makan-makan

as_extracts.name: LIND7108-E05
as_extracts.description: They use familiar language, modelled sentences and grammatical structures to create texts appropriate to audience.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: interact with others using modelled language to exchange information in familiar contexts about themselves and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the appropriate terms of address, for example, Selamat pagi Ibu Dewi, Selamat siang Bapak Jim or talking with a classmate using Kamu berasal dari mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in regular classroom interactions such as responding to Apa kabar? Sudah makan? Dari mana? or taking leave, for example, permisi Bu; selamat jalan; sampai besok; silakan; terima kasih

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging personal details in simulated interviews, classroom interactions, and responding to questions, for example, Kenalkan, nama saya … dan saya berasal dari Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and responding to information about their personal and immediate worlds through guessing games and card games, for example, Apakah saya penyanyi?; Boleh saya minta pisang?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled language to ask and respond to questions from their peers about their daily routine, school and home environment, for example, Bagaimana rumah kamu?; Naik apa ke sekolah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with peers to express likes, dislikes and preferences, and to exchange and explain opinions, for example, Saya lebih suka bermain bola basket daripada sepak bola; Saya paling suka belajar bahasa Indonesia karena menarik

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled or formulaic language structures to extend interactions, for example, … yang …; … tetapi …; … dengan cepat …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous interjections and exclamations to show interest, comprehension and fill pauses, for example, Oh ya (with nod), oke, baik, baiklah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class about themselves, their family, pets, likes and dislikes, hobbies and leisure activities; creating a graph representing the information they collected; and using the graph to make simple remarks about the class

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines and tasks related to their classroom and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using expressions of well-wishing for appropriate dates, celebrations and occasions, for example, Selamat hari ulang tahun! Selamat makan!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in classroom routines and activities using expressions such as Sudah siap?; Sudah selesai?; Belum?; Tutup pintu!; Buka buku tulismu!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions to clarify meaning, and requesting information, explanation or help, for example, Maaf; Apa … dalam bahasa Indonesia?; Bu, boleh minta …?; Boleh minta tolong?; Apa artinya?; Boleh pinjam penamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a ‘find your partner’ or ‘find someone who …’ game on the theme of pastimes or routines, for example, Apa hobi kamu? Hobi saya memancing di sungai; Kamu melakukan apa pada hari Senin? Saya ikut klub catur

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing aspects of school and social life, and the behaviour expected in Indonesian classrooms, for example, Kelas di sekolah Indonesia punya ketua dan wakil ketua kelas, and responding respectfully to others’ contributions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a real or simulated visit to an Indonesian home or restaurant, using culturally appropriate expressions, for example, permisi, silakan, assalamuailaikum, tambah lagi

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in scenarios, for example, being lost and asking for and giving directions, jalan terus; belok ke kiri; belok ke kanan sampai ke Jalan …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a role-play to exchange information on familiar topics such as buying clothes in a shop or discussing what outfits they are wearing as they get ready to go to a party

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in real or simulated interactions relating to negotiating for services such as transport, ordering food or goods, for example, Mau membeli bakso?; Mau menonton film atau bermain sepak bola nanti sore?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising a real or imagined shopping visit to bargain for souvenirs, for example, Maaf ada baju batik?; Berapa harganya? Bisa kurang?; Wah, terlalu mahal! Saya rugi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving, accepting or declining invitations, including making excuses to avoid causing offence or embarrassment, for example, Mau ikut ke …? Terima kasih, saya tidak bisa; Maaf, ya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to prepare a notice or email to advertise an event such as a celebration, sports event or competition

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating and making decisions about whole class activities, for example, Bagaimana kalau kita …; Mengapa tidak?; Kelas mau bermain … atau …?; Ayo, kita …; … ide bagus!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging details such as time, place, activity and participants when organising real or imagined events, using texts such as phone conversations, emails and text messages, for example, Jam berapa?; Di mana?; Hari apa?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM06 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts such as a profile, montage or avatar, choosing what aspects to share about themselves, for example, Nama saya Emily. Saya dari Geelong, Australia. Saya bersekolah di SMP … Hobi saya berselancar dan mendengarkan musik. Saya suka menonton film tetapi saya kurang suka film horor karena menakutkan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing an email to introduce themselves to a real or imagined Indonesian host family, providing personal information, preferences and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school or a guide to their favourite place

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing a typical day during the school week or on the weekend (using sudah, belum and sedang to indicate tense) by writing a diary entry or letter to a family member or friend

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with students in a buddy school who are learning English (respecting privacy guidelines), and making choices about when to use Indonesian or English depending on the context, topic and nature of the interaction

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or brochure in Indonesian for travel to their local area, including what to see and do, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and wear, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names and history

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing and performing dialogues between characters using appropriate textual conventions for opening, maintaining and closing a conversation, for example, a talk-show host interviewing a famous musician; a market-stall vendor bargaining with a customer; 2 characters in a short drama or skit

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using key words or expressions to compose a description of characters or events in different types of imaginative texts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using secure digital tools to create a video clip or photo story based on imaginary characters, places and events

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing profiles of celebrities or significant people who speak Indonesian such as Jessica Mauboy, Chris Hemsworth, Barack Obama, creating a narrative using a written version of telinga panjang, with each class member contributing to the text when it is their turn, for example, a story starting with ‘Saya senang sekali karena …’

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E01 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cardinal numbers to count (e.g. puluh, belas, ratus, ribu, juta); using ordinal numbers to sequence order, for example, pertama, ke+number

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating quantity using plurals, for example, tiga buku; banyak buku; buku-buku

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking ideas using conjunctions, for example, dan, karena, tetapi, atau, dengan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using imperatives, for example, Bacalah!; Tulislah!; Dengarkanlah!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing simple actions using base words, for example, makan; minum; pulang; pergi; suka; tidur; noticing ber- and me- verbs

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to existence/presence/possession, for example, ada, tidak ada; Ibu ada kelas; Dia punya bola; Ada dua lapangan bola basket di sekolah tetapi tidak ada kolam renang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to give directions and information about location, for example, di/ke, dari, di sini, di sana, di atas, di bawah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to the present, past and future using time indicators such as hari ini; sekarang; kemarin; sebelum; sesudah; besok

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing modality, for example, bisa; harus; boleh; mau

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using duplication to indicate extended or repeated action, for example, berjalan-jalan; bermalas-malas; duduk-duduk; makan-makan

as_extracts.name: LIND7108-E06
as_extracts.description: Students begin to use pronunciation, intonation and rhythm in spoken Indonesian to develop fluency.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken Indonesian to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the sound of Indonesian is represented using the Roman alphabet

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the Indonesian alphabet to spell out names or expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the pronunciation of the Indonesian alphabet modelled by the teacher or audio scripts and participating in activities such as spelling words out loud, games using letter patterns or hotel check-in scenarios, for example, d-e-w-i

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating modelled phrases and sentences using Indonesian rhythm and intonation, for example, Terima kasih; Saya membaca buku; Saya naik becak ke sekolah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the distinctive sounds and sound combinations of Indonesian (e.g. namanya, mau, baik, umur, tinggal, membaca) by listening to short audio or video texts and tracking how many sound combinations they can hear

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising intonation for questions (with or without question words), statements, commands and interjections (e.g. Wah!; Aduh!; Oh begitu!; Sudah makan?; Sudah makan) by listening to audio and video clips for the target phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading out loud to develop correct pronunciation, intonation, rhythm and stress by participating in reading games and races

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some informal variants and understanding the appropriate settings for their use, such as makasih instead of terima kasih, and participating in short skits where the language is used in both correct and incorrect contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning sentences (e.g. identifying and describing mystery objects as they are lifted out of a box) using the demonstratives ini/itu, for example, Ini buku saya; Itu temannya

as_extracts.name: LIND7108-E07
as_extracts.description: They demonstrate understanding that Indonesian has conventions for non-verbal, spoken and written communication.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM01 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: interact with others using modelled language to exchange information in familiar contexts about themselves and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the appropriate terms of address, for example, Selamat pagi Ibu Dewi, Selamat siang Bapak Jim or talking with a classmate using Kamu berasal dari mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in regular classroom interactions such as responding to Apa kabar? Sudah makan? Dari mana? or taking leave, for example, permisi Bu; selamat jalan; sampai besok; silakan; terima kasih

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging personal details in simulated interviews, classroom interactions, and responding to questions, for example, Kenalkan, nama saya … dan saya berasal dari Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and responding to information about their personal and immediate worlds through guessing games and card games, for example, Apakah saya penyanyi?; Boleh saya minta pisang?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled language to ask and respond to questions from their peers about their daily routine, school and home environment, for example, Bagaimana rumah kamu?; Naik apa ke sekolah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with peers to express likes, dislikes and preferences, and to exchange and explain opinions, for example, Saya lebih suka bermain bola basket daripada sepak bola; Saya paling suka belajar bahasa Indonesia karena menarik

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled or formulaic language structures to extend interactions, for example, … yang …; … tetapi …; … dengan cepat …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous interjections and exclamations to show interest, comprehension and fill pauses, for example, Oh ya (with nod), oke, baik, baiklah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class about themselves, their family, pets, likes and dislikes, hobbies and leisure activities; creating a graph representing the information they collected; and using the graph to make simple remarks about the class

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM05 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to Indonesian texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in Indonesian in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using skills that promote reading for understanding by, for example, identifying all the words they understand in an Indonesian sentence or words that are similar in Indonesian and English, to help make an ‘educated guess’ about the meaning of the sentence

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing strategies to interpret body language and non-verbal cues, for example, senam and teacher gestures and creating and performing a short comedy skit demonstrating miscommunications

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled texts such as cloze passages or songs in dictation exercises to develop listening for understanding

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting Indonesian gestures to convey meaning and using them appropriately in classroom interactions with peers and teachers, for example, only using the right hand to pass objects, using the thumb to point

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dictionaries or online translation tools to find meaning of words or expressions and using context to assist understanding, for example, using context to determine whether halus is referring to refined behaviour, smooth texture or a well-crafted object

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of a text, including versions created by online translators, and discussing any issues that emerge

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prior knowledge to access culture-specific vocabulary and images to interpret meaning, for example, using a music video to understand song lyrics

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring, expanding and consolidating word usage using online translation tools to interpret idioms, proverbs, sayings and set phrases, for example, Jam karet; Sedia payung sebelum hujan; Rajin pangkal pandai, hemat pangkal kaya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print and online dictionaries, selecting appropriate meaning from alternatives provided and comparing translations with peers, explaining cultural references and expressions and any aspects ‘lost in translation’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying ‘false friends’ or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in Indonesian that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM06 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts such as a profile, montage or avatar, choosing what aspects to share about themselves, for example, Nama saya Emily. Saya dari Geelong, Australia. Saya bersekolah di SMP … Hobi saya berselancar dan mendengarkan musik. Saya suka menonton film tetapi saya kurang suka film horor karena menakutkan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing an email to introduce themselves to a real or imagined Indonesian host family, providing personal information, preferences and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school or a guide to their favourite place

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing a typical day during the school week or on the weekend (using sudah, belum and sedang to indicate tense) by writing a diary entry or letter to a family member or friend

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with students in a buddy school who are learning English (respecting privacy guidelines), and making choices about when to use Indonesian or English depending on the context, topic and nature of the interaction

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or brochure in Indonesian for travel to their local area, including what to see and do, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and wear, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names and history

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing and performing dialogues between characters using appropriate textual conventions for opening, maintaining and closing a conversation, for example, a talk-show host interviewing a famous musician; a market-stall vendor bargaining with a customer; 2 characters in a short drama or skit

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using key words or expressions to compose a description of characters or events in different types of imaginative texts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using secure digital tools to create a video clip or photo story based on imaginary characters, places and events

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing profiles of celebrities or significant people who speak Indonesian such as Jessica Mauboy, Chris Hemsworth, Barack Obama, creating a narrative using a written version of telinga panjang, with each class member contributing to the text when it is their turn, for example, a story starting with ‘Saya senang sekali karena …’

content_descriptions.text: compare the structures and features of Indonesian with English and/or other languages using some metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding subject+verb+object sentence construction in Indonesian and English and comparing with other languages, noting word order of nouns and adjectives and the absence of the verb ‘to be’; identifying loan words, for example, taksi, om, salam; highlighting these elements in an Indonesian text and discussing with classmates

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: annotating texts with coloured highlighters to identify grammatical elements and features that are unique to Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian uses adverbs of time and frequency to indicate tense, whereas English uses verb conjugation (e.g. sedang, sudah, belum) and creating a comparative chart

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian uses prefixes and suffixes to change the meaning of words, for example, me-, ber-, -an, pe-an, -lah, and comparing this with the role of affixes in English and other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian uses classifiers such as kota, pulau and pantai to categorise a place and using this to create annotations or captions on an image or map

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing similarities and differences in key features of Indonesian texts such as stories, songs and conversations with comparable texts in English and/or other languages and creating lists of these features to create personal glossaries

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the exchange of terms between Indonesian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages such as the use of Makassan terms in Yolngu, for example, balanda; rupiah; nenek

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing the position and/or location of Indonesia in Indonesian compared with the lands of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples in northern Australia on a map of Australasia

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the exchange of terms between Indonesian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages such as the use of Makassan terms in Yolngu, for example, balanda, rupiah, nenek; being aware that the classroom may have representations of different languages and cultures (e.g. Saya berbicara bahasa Arab dengan kakek dan nenek); and surveying students about what language(s) they connect with to create a class chart

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: appreciating that elements of Indonesian culture such as gotong royong, halus, sombong and sopan santun are reflected through behaviour and attitudes, viewing a short video clip and identifying, observing and discussing these behaviours

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching how cultural expectations for travellers vary across Indonesia, discussing the reasons for these practices and creating a ‘dos and don’ts’ list for travellers, for example, Di candi Borobudur sebaiknya Anda memakai rok panjang; Jangan berenang dengan baju renang yang berwarna hijau di pantai Parangtritis

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing music video clips and discussing how aspects of language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values are represented in the lyrics, music and visual elements

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Indonesian terms for siblings focus on relative ages rather than gender, discussing the underlying attitudes and values this suggests and comparing with English and other languages spoken by members of the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing examples of traditional and contemporary images or texts in print and online, and comparing how representations of identity and gender in the language have changed over time

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interact with others using modelled language to exchange information in familiar contexts about themselves and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the appropriate terms of address, for example, Selamat pagi Ibu Dewi, Selamat siang Bapak Jim or talking with a classmate using Kamu berasal dari mana?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in regular classroom interactions such as responding to Apa kabar? Sudah makan? Dari mana? or taking leave, for example, permisi Bu; selamat jalan; sampai besok; silakan; terima kasih

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging personal details in simulated interviews, classroom interactions, and responding to questions, for example, Kenalkan, nama saya … dan saya berasal dari Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and responding to information about their personal and immediate worlds through guessing games and card games, for example, Apakah saya penyanyi?; Boleh saya minta pisang?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled language to ask and respond to questions from their peers about their daily routine, school and home environment, for example, Bagaimana rumah kamu?; Naik apa ke sekolah?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with peers to express likes, dislikes and preferences, and to exchange and explain opinions, for example, Saya lebih suka bermain bola basket daripada sepak bola; Saya paling suka belajar bahasa Indonesia karena menarik

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled or formulaic language structures to extend interactions, for example, … yang …; … tetapi …; … dengan cepat …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous interjections and exclamations to show interest, comprehension and fill pauses, for example, Oh ya (with nod), oke, baik, baiklah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class about themselves, their family, pets, likes and dislikes, hobbies and leisure activities; creating a graph representing the information they collected; and using the graph to make simple remarks about the class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines and tasks related to their classroom and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using expressions of well-wishing for appropriate dates, celebrations and occasions, for example, Selamat hari ulang tahun! Selamat makan!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in classroom routines and activities using expressions such as Sudah siap?; Sudah selesai?; Belum?; Tutup pintu!; Buka buku tulismu!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions to clarify meaning, and requesting information, explanation or help, for example, Maaf; Apa … dalam bahasa Indonesia?; Bu, boleh minta …?; Boleh minta tolong?; Apa artinya?; Boleh pinjam penamu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a ‘find your partner’ or ‘find someone who …’ game on the theme of pastimes or routines, for example, Apa hobi kamu? Hobi saya memancing di sungai; Kamu melakukan apa pada hari Senin? Saya ikut klub catur

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing aspects of school and social life, and the behaviour expected in Indonesian classrooms, for example, Kelas di sekolah Indonesia punya ketua dan wakil ketua kelas, and responding respectfully to others’ contributions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a real or simulated visit to an Indonesian home or restaurant, using culturally appropriate expressions, for example, permisi, silakan, assalamuailaikum, tambah lagi

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in scenarios, for example, being lost and asking for and giving directions, jalan terus; belok ke kiri; belok ke kanan sampai ke Jalan …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a role-play to exchange information on familiar topics such as buying clothes in a shop or discussing what outfits they are wearing as they get ready to go to a party

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in real or simulated interactions relating to negotiating for services such as transport, ordering food or goods, for example, Mau membeli bakso?; Mau menonton film atau bermain sepak bola nanti sore?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising a real or imagined shopping visit to bargain for souvenirs, for example, Maaf ada baju batik?; Berapa harganya? Bisa kurang?; Wah, terlalu mahal! Saya rugi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving, accepting or declining invitations, including making excuses to avoid causing offence or embarrassment, for example, Mau ikut ke …? Terima kasih, saya tidak bisa; Maaf, ya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to prepare a notice or email to advertise an event such as a celebration, sports event or competition

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating and making decisions about whole class activities, for example, Bagaimana kalau kita …; Mengapa tidak?; Kelas mau bermain … atau …?; Ayo, kita …; … ide bagus!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging details such as time, place, activity and participants when organising real or imagined events, using texts such as phone conversations, emails and text messages, for example, Jam berapa?; Di mana?; Hari apa?

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM04 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to teacher-modified texts, videos or audio and responding to true-or-false questions using ya, bukan, benar, salah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing familiar texts to identify specific information, for example, infographics, text messages and teacher-curated social media posts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing texts (e.g. signs, advertisements or artworks) and extracting information to answer questions or create short texts such as captions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, classifying and summarising information such as results of class surveys (e.g. 30% murid suka berolahraga air, 40% suka berlibur di gunung) and using questions, for example, Kamu suka makan apa?; Kamu suka pergi ke mana pada akhir minggu?; Apa binatang favoritmu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching and comparing different types of eating venues in Indonesia such as rumah makan Padang, warung, kaki lima, restoran to make menu selections, for example, Mau mencoba makanan apa? Mau mencoba minuman apa? Sudah makan rendang?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing cartoons, comics and stories, and expressing opinions and ideas, for example, Saya suka / kurang suka; Saya rasa / pikir; Pada pendapat saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching information to develop an itinerary for an imagined holiday using modelled vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, for example, Berangkat dari Jakarta jam 08:00; Sampai di Makassar jam 11:00; Pada hari Senin ikut tur ke obyek wisata Rammang-Rammang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: navigating secure online applications to find out about transport and services in Indonesia, using information in a simulated conversation with a taxi driver or person in a hotel, for example, Berapa tarif dua malam di hotel?; Bagaimana fasilitas kamar/hotel?; Apakah termasuk makan pagi?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a film or video and writing a summary of the plot or a profile of a character, Saya suka ceritanya karena dramatis; Bayu tinggal di Jakarta dan dia suka bermain sepak bola

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM04-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching a topic of interest in Indonesian and presenting information using modelled vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions, for example, creating an infographic; writing a short report for the school newsletter; creating a digital presentation for the class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM05 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to Indonesian texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in Indonesian in familiar contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using skills that promote reading for understanding by, for example, identifying all the words they understand in an Indonesian sentence or words that are similar in Indonesian and English, to help make an ‘educated guess’ about the meaning of the sentence

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing strategies to interpret body language and non-verbal cues, for example, senam and teacher gestures and creating and performing a short comedy skit demonstrating miscommunications

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled texts such as cloze passages or songs in dictation exercises to develop listening for understanding

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting Indonesian gestures to convey meaning and using them appropriately in classroom interactions with peers and teachers, for example, only using the right hand to pass objects, using the thumb to point

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dictionaries or online translation tools to find meaning of words or expressions and using context to assist understanding, for example, using context to determine whether halus is referring to refined behaviour, smooth texture or a well-crafted object

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of a text, including versions created by online translators, and discussing any issues that emerge

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prior knowledge to access culture-specific vocabulary and images to interpret meaning, for example, using a music video to understand song lyrics

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring, expanding and consolidating word usage using online translation tools to interpret idioms, proverbs, sayings and set phrases, for example, Jam karet; Sedia payung sebelum hujan; Rajin pangkal pandai, hemat pangkal kaya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print and online dictionaries, selecting appropriate meaning from alternatives provided and comparing translations with peers, explaining cultural references and expressions and any aspects ‘lost in translation’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying ‘false friends’ or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in Indonesian that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8CM06 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts such as a profile, montage or avatar, choosing what aspects to share about themselves, for example, Nama saya Emily. Saya dari Geelong, Australia. Saya bersekolah di SMP … Hobi saya berselancar dan mendengarkan musik. Saya suka menonton film tetapi saya kurang suka film horor karena menakutkan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing an email to introduce themselves to a real or imagined Indonesian host family, providing personal information, preferences and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school or a guide to their favourite place

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing a typical day during the school week or on the weekend (using sudah, belum and sedang to indicate tense) by writing a diary entry or letter to a family member or friend

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with students in a buddy school who are learning English (respecting privacy guidelines), and making choices about when to use Indonesian or English depending on the context, topic and nature of the interaction

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or brochure in Indonesian for travel to their local area, including what to see and do, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and wear, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names and history

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing and performing dialogues between characters using appropriate textual conventions for opening, maintaining and closing a conversation, for example, a talk-show host interviewing a famous musician; a market-stall vendor bargaining with a customer; 2 characters in a short drama or skit

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using key words or expressions to compose a description of characters or events in different types of imaginative texts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using secure digital tools to create a video clip or photo story based on imaginary characters, places and events

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8CM06-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing profiles of celebrities or significant people who speak Indonesian such as Jessica Mauboy, Chris Hemsworth, Barack Obama, creating a narrative using a written version of telinga panjang, with each class member contributing to the text when it is their turn, for example, a story starting with ‘Saya senang sekali karena …’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken Indonesian to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the sound of Indonesian is represented using the Roman alphabet

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the Indonesian alphabet to spell out names or expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the pronunciation of the Indonesian alphabet modelled by the teacher or audio scripts and participating in activities such as spelling words out loud, games using letter patterns or hotel check-in scenarios, for example, d-e-w-i

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating modelled phrases and sentences using Indonesian rhythm and intonation, for example, Terima kasih; Saya membaca buku; Saya naik becak ke sekolah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the distinctive sounds and sound combinations of Indonesian (e.g. namanya, mau, baik, umur, tinggal, membaca) by listening to short audio or video texts and tracking how many sound combinations they can hear

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising intonation for questions (with or without question words), statements, commands and interjections (e.g. Wah!; Aduh!; Oh begitu!; Sudah makan?; Sudah makan) by listening to audio and video clips for the target phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading out loud to develop correct pronunciation, intonation, rhythm and stress by participating in reading games and races

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some informal variants and understanding the appropriate settings for their use, such as makasih instead of terima kasih, and participating in short skits where the language is used in both correct and incorrect contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning sentences (e.g. identifying and describing mystery objects as they are lifted out of a box) using the demonstratives ini/itu, for example, Ini buku saya; Itu temannya

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using subject+verb+object modelled sentence structures (e.g. Saya belajar bahasa Indonesia) and using correct word order noun+adjectives to describe qualities of nouns such as people, objects and places, for example, komputer baru, sepatu bagus, anjing besar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct word order for possessive pronouns such as saya/aku/ku, Anda/kamu/mu, dia/nya, mereka, for example, nama saya …; pena dia …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing qualities, for example, lebih … daripada

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using interrogatives playing a game of 20 questions, for example, siapa; apa; bagaimana; berapa; dari mana; di mana; ke mana; apakah; kapan; jam berapa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negating using tidak, bukan and belum, for example, Sudah siap? Belum; Saya tidak punya buku; Mereka bukan teman saya

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cardinal numbers to count (e.g. puluh, belas, ratus, ribu, juta); using ordinal numbers to sequence order, for example, pertama, ke+number

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating quantity using plurals, for example, tiga buku; banyak buku; buku-buku

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking ideas using conjunctions, for example, dan, karena, tetapi, atau, dengan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using imperatives, for example, Bacalah!; Tulislah!; Dengarkanlah!

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing simple actions using base words, for example, makan; minum; pulang; pergi; suka; tidur; noticing ber- and me- verbs

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to existence/presence/possession, for example, ada, tidak ada; Ibu ada kelas; Dia punya bola; Ada dua lapangan bola basket di sekolah tetapi tidak ada kolam renang

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to give directions and information about location, for example, di/ke, dari, di sini, di sana, di atas, di bawah

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to the present, past and future using time indicators such as hari ini; sekarang; kemarin; sebelum; sesudah; besok

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing modality, for example, bisa; harus; boleh; mau

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using duplication to indicate extended or repeated action, for example, berjalan-jalan; bermalas-malas; duduk-duduk; makan-makan

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare the structures and features of Indonesian with English and/or other languages using some metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding subject+verb+object sentence construction in Indonesian and English and comparing with other languages, noting word order of nouns and adjectives and the absence of the verb ‘to be’; identifying loan words, for example, taksi, om, salam; highlighting these elements in an Indonesian text and discussing with classmates

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: annotating texts with coloured highlighters to identify grammatical elements and features that are unique to Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian uses adverbs of time and frequency to indicate tense, whereas English uses verb conjugation (e.g. sedang, sudah, belum) and creating a comparative chart

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian uses prefixes and suffixes to change the meaning of words, for example, me-, ber-, -an, pe-an, -lah, and comparing this with the role of affixes in English and other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesian uses classifiers such as kota, pulau and pantai to categorise a place and using this to create annotations or captions on an image or map

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing similarities and differences in key features of Indonesian texts such as stories, songs and conversations with comparable texts in English and/or other languages and creating lists of these features to create personal glossaries

elaborations.name: VC2LIN8UL03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the exchange of terms between Indonesian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages such as the use of Makassan terms in Yolngu, for example, balanda; rupiah; nenek

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN8UL04 - Indonesian

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 9 and 10, Indonesian language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students use Indonesian to initiate and sustain interactions while sharing their own and others’ experiences of the world. They listen, speak, read, write and view to communicate with other speakers of Indonesian in local and global settings through authentic community and moderated, secure online events. They continue to receive guidance, modelling, feedback and support from their peers and teachers. 

Students use authentic and purpose-developed resources, increasingly of their own choice, to access and/or create a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, which may include textbooks, audio and video clips, magazines and images, online and print articles, and teacher-moderated social media. They acknowledge that there are diverse influences on communication and cultural identity, and that these influences can shape their own behaviours, values and beliefs.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 10, students initiate and sustain Indonesian to exchange and compare ideas and experiences about their own and others’ personal worlds. They communicate using spoken and written language to collaborate, plan and reflect on activities and events. They interpret and analyse information and ideas in texts and demonstrate their understanding of different perspectives. They identify and evaluate information and respond in Indonesian or English, adjusting their language to convey meaning and to suit context, purpose and audience. They use structures and features of non-verbal, spoken and written Indonesian to create texts.

Students apply features and conventions of spoken Indonesian to enhance fluency. They select and apply knowledge of language conventions, structures and features to interact, make meaning from, and create spoken and written texts appropriate to different levels of formality. They discuss the structures and features of Indonesian texts using metalanguage. They reflect on their own language use and cultural identity, and draw on their experience of learning Indonesian, to discuss how this influences their ideas and ways of communicating.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E02 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E05 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing sentence structures in Indonesian, English and/or other languages they know, and recognising the use of different structures and features used to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E08 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with Indonesian-speaking peers in Indonesia and Australia through email, shared secure digital spaces or video, comparing topics of interest, language choices and expressions

elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining to others a procedure or practice such as a recipe, the rules of a sport or board game, instructions on keeping a pet/animal, or fashion tips, for example, Tambahkan dua sendok makan susu kental manis; Bersihkan kandang hamster setiap hari

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL02 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adjectives of character to describe the qualities of people by playing a Who is it? game, for example, murah hati, besar kepala

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating tense and time using specific time markers, for example, sekali-sekali, belum pernah, tidak pernah, tadi malam, nanti sore, pada masa depan, dua tahun yang lalu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating possibility (e.g. mungkin; mudah-mudahan; semoga; saya harap) when writing ‘a letter to my 21-year-old self’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: specifying what is being referred to using yang and … nya, for example, yang ini, yang itu, Yang mana? in a shopping role-play; Cuacanya panas sekali hari ini in a diary entry

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using yang in embedded clauses, for example, viewing images and creating captions that contain embedded clauses such as Binatang yang terancam punah termasuk koala dan harimau Sumatra

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating equivalence using adalah, for example, Buku itu adalah buku latihan bahasa Indonesia kelas kami

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has base words and that word families are created using affixation (e.g. belajar; mengajar; pelajaran; pengajaran; pengajar; pelajar) by playing digital or online matching games with word pairs

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: adding affixation ke … an to base words to create abstract nouns (e.g. kesehatan; kegiatan; kehidupan) or to indicate that someone or something is affected by the base word, for example, kehujanan; kepanasan; kelaparan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating action using transitive verbs, me- verbs and understanding the function of suffixes, for example, me … kan; me … I; Jono menaiki gunung; Jono menaikkan bendera; Saya membeli makanan di pasar; Saya membelikan ibu makanan di pasar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using di- forms to emphasise the object, for example, Buku dibaca oleh in contrast to Dia membaca buku; Komputernya diambil dari kantor sekolah in contrast to Dia mengambil komputernya dari kantor

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the person doing an action using pe- prefix, for example, penjual, penari, pelukis

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the preposition kepada for written exchanges with people and giving things to people, for example, Dia memberi uang kepada adiknya; Saya bertanya kepada guru saya tentang masalah itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using comparatives such as the prefix se- (e.g. sebesar; Dia setinggi adiknya) or lebih … daripada … (e.g. lebih murah … dari pada …) and superlatives ter …, yang paling … (e.g. Stadion itu adalah stadion yang terbesar di seluruh dunia; Dia penyanyi yang paling populer di dunia)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking information using interrogatives and question forms playing 20 questions or a Who is it? game, for example, mengapa/kenapa, bagaimana, yang mana, untuk apa/siapa, dengan apa/siapa, berapa, dari mana

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjunctions to create complex sentences (e.g. supaya/sehingga; namun demikian; walaupun; meskipun; sementara/sambil/sedangkan), for example, in a class debate or writing an evaluative or persuasive article for a school magazine

as_extracts.description: They use structures and features of non-verbal, spoken and written Indonesian to create texts.

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-play scenarios related to life in Indonesia, such as living with a host family, seeking medical treatment, planning a day out with Indonesian friends, for example, Saya minta obat untuk masuk angin; Ke mana besok?; Kita bertemu di mal pada jam 10

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and completing tasks involving authentic or simulated transactions such as planning a holiday or purchasing goods (e.g. Bagaimana kalau kami ke Danau Toba?; Bisa tawar-menawar?), including culturally appropriate non-verbal gestures to accompany dialogue

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to decide responsibilities and roles in a class activity, for example, discussing with classmates what to include in a travel brochure, aspects of an Indonesian history presentation or a multimodal presentation on a school issue, for example, Sebaiknya kita mengumpulkan informasi dulu; Bolehkah kita membuat video daripada poster?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E04 - Indonesian

elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing reflections on their experience of learning Indonesian, discussing progress, challenges and achievements

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E02 - Indonesian
