elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating possibility (e.g. mungkin; mudah-mudahan; semoga; saya harap) when writing ‘a letter to my 21-year-old self’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: specifying what is being referred to using yang and … nya, for example, yang ini, yang itu, Yang mana? in a shopping role-play; Cuacanya panas sekali hari ini in a diary entry

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using yang in embedded clauses, for example, viewing images and creating captions that contain embedded clauses such as Binatang yang terancam punah termasuk koala dan harimau Sumatra

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating equivalence using adalah, for example, Buku itu adalah buku latihan bahasa Indonesia kelas kami

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has base words and that word families are created using affixation (e.g. belajar; mengajar; pelajaran; pengajaran; pengajar; pelajar) by playing digital or online matching games with word pairs

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: adding affixation ke … an to base words to create abstract nouns (e.g. kesehatan; kegiatan; kehidupan) or to indicate that someone or something is affected by the base word, for example, kehujanan; kepanasan; kelaparan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating action using transitive verbs, me- verbs and understanding the function of suffixes, for example, me … kan; me … I; Jono menaiki gunung; Jono menaikkan bendera; Saya membeli makanan di pasar; Saya membelikan ibu makanan di pasar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using di- forms to emphasise the object, for example, Buku dibaca oleh in contrast to Dia membaca buku; Komputernya diambil dari kantor sekolah in contrast to Dia mengambil komputernya dari kantor

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the person doing an action using pe- prefix, for example, penjual, penari, pelukis

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the preposition kepada for written exchanges with people and giving things to people, for example, Dia memberi uang kepada adiknya; Saya bertanya kepada guru saya tentang masalah itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using comparatives such as the prefix se- (e.g. sebesar; Dia setinggi adiknya) or lebih … daripada … (e.g. lebih murah … dari pada …) and superlatives ter …, yang paling … (e.g. Stadion itu adalah stadion yang terbesar di seluruh dunia; Dia penyanyi yang paling populer di dunia)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking information using interrogatives and question forms playing 20 questions or a Who is it? game, for example, mengapa/kenapa, bagaimana, yang mana, untuk apa/siapa, dengan apa/siapa, berapa, dari mana

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjunctions to create complex sentences (e.g. supaya/sehingga; namun demikian; walaupun; meskipun; sementara/sambil/sedangkan), for example, in a class debate or writing an evaluative or persuasive article for a school magazine

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E02 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E06 - Indonesian

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing empathy, well-wishing or recognition of success, for example, Kasihan!; Wah, hebat!; Selamat!; Semoga sukses dalam ujian/kompetisi …; Semoga cepat sembuh

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous interjections and exclamations to show interest, comprehension and fill pauses, for example, Hebaaat!; Asyik!; Oh, begitu!; Apa ya?; Begini …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating through secure digital spaces such as text messages using informal abbreviations, for example, gk; ku; krn; dgn

organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.

elaborations.elaboration_text: using di- forms to emphasise the object, for example, Buku dibaca oleh in contrast to Dia membaca buku; Komputernya diambil dari kantor sekolah in contrast to Dia mengambil komputernya dari kantor

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the person doing an action using pe- prefix, for example, penjual, penari, pelukis

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the preposition kepada for written exchanges with people and giving things to people, for example, Dia memberi uang kepada adiknya; Saya bertanya kepada guru saya tentang masalah itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using comparatives such as the prefix se- (e.g. sebesar; Dia setinggi adiknya) or lebih … daripada … (e.g. lebih murah … dari pada …) and superlatives ter …, yang paling … (e.g. Stadion itu adalah stadion yang terbesar di seluruh dunia; Dia penyanyi yang paling populer di dunia)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking information using interrogatives and question forms playing 20 questions or a Who is it? game, for example, mengapa/kenapa, bagaimana, yang mana, untuk apa/siapa, dengan apa/siapa, berapa, dari mana

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjunctions to create complex sentences (e.g. supaya/sehingga; namun demikian; walaupun; meskipun; sementara/sambil/sedangkan), for example, in a class debate or writing an evaluative or persuasive article for a school magazine

as_extracts.name: LIND71010-E08
as_extracts.description: They discuss the structures and features of Indonesian texts using metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate Indonesian texts, using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how texts are constructed, including cohesive devices such as conjunctions, and coherence devices such as time markers (e.g. Mula-Mula …, Kedua …, Akhirnya …, Di satu pihak …, Di pihak lain …) and comparing with English and/or other languages, creating a comparative table for their personal glossary

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining language structures and features used in a range of texts for communicative effect (e.g. to inform, entertain or persuade), reading short passages and highlighting examples of the target structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on literary devices to enhance ideas such as metaphors in texts (e.g. adalah and simile), for example, sama dengan; seperti; setinggi; bagai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the prevalence of acronyms known as singkatan (e.g. met ultah, PenJas, narkoba, Jatim), and comparing them with English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in register of language used in texts, and noticing variations such as colloquial language and how it differs from standard forms, creating a chart showing the different forms and adding it to their personal glossary, for example, Kasih aku coklat, dong!; Boleh minta coklat, Bu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying loan words in spoken Indonesian, for example, ngopi; dirilis; meng-upload

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing sentence structures in Indonesian, English and/or other languages they know, and recognising the use of different structures and features used to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and discussing how the linguistic diversity of Indonesia reveals cultural diversity, and recognising how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting that Indonesian speakers may use gender-neutral language such as pacar, dia and -nya, and that these cannot be translated with equivalence without contextual cues

as_extracts.name: LIND71010-E09
as_extracts.description: They reflect on their own language use and cultural identity, and draw on their experience of learning Indonesian, to discuss how this influences their ideas and ways of communicating.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10CM03 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: use spoken and written exchanges to discuss, plan and reflect on activities, events and experiences with peers

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-play scenarios related to life in Indonesia, such as living with a host family, seeking medical treatment, planning a day out with Indonesian friends, for example, Saya minta obat untuk masuk angin; Ke mana besok?; Kita bertemu di mal pada jam 10

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and completing tasks involving authentic or simulated transactions such as planning a holiday or purchasing goods (e.g. Bagaimana kalau kami ke Danau Toba?; Bisa tawar-menawar?), including culturally appropriate non-verbal gestures to accompany dialogue

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to decide responsibilities and roles in a class activity, for example, discussing with classmates what to include in a travel brochure, aspects of an Indonesian history presentation or a multimodal presentation on a school issue, for example, Sebaiknya kita mengumpulkan informasi dulu; Bolehkah kita membuat video daripada poster?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in simulated scenarios, for example, enquiring about student exchange programs or interviewing for a scholarship, including culturally appropriate non-verbal gestures to accompany dialogue

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the success of a school activity, excursion or event using a collaborative secure digital format to provide feedback, for example, Saya suka menyanyi lagu …; Saya senang pergi ke galeri karena …; Bagaimana pendapat kamu tentang Museum …?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the comments function on a shared document or posting replies to a post on a secure digital platform to create collaborative texts such as a poster advertising a class party or a storybook to read to a buddy class in a primary school, for example, Apa itu, panjat pinang?; Seharusnya kita minta izin dulu kalau pakai foto dia?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing reflections on their experience of learning Indonesian, discussing progress, challenges and achievements

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL04 - Indonesian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: being aware that there are regional and social differences regarding norms of interaction across Indonesia and reflecting that geographical and social differences also influence norms of interaction in Australia and other countries

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK2
organising_ideas.text: The interrelationships between people and the diverse environments and systems across the Asia region have global implications.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that many expressions and behaviours, such as meeting a friend at a suitable time, are closely related to cultural and religious practices and beliefs (e.g. Saya sholat dulu; Ada upacara potong gigi di pura; Ada kebaktian di gereja; Mau beli jamu dulu), and reading texts or viewing short video clips that outline these cultural practices and discussing within the class

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesia has a diversity of languages (using a map to create a visual representation of language use), people may be multilingual and that languages are always evolving and changing, for example, bahasa Jawa; bahasa Gaul; bahasa Binan

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing personal journal entries and participating in group discussions to reflect on and evaluate how learning Indonesian has had an impact on their own assumptions about Indonesian language, culture and identity

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring intercultural communication, considering how their own cultural ways of thinking and behaving affect attitudes and influence other people’s responses or interpretations and how they change over time

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and explaining the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place, to present in Indonesian to a group of Indonesian-speaking visitors at a school assembly

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the influence of language (e.g. noticing how language is used in art, graffiti, online mediums and political protests), and reflecting on how messaging used in public spaces about Reformasi; Keluarga Berencana; Satu nusa, satu bangsa, satu Bahasa, can have an impact on national behaviours and identity

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the influence of activists, artists and authors on language, art and ways of thinking and how they may influence attitudes and values regarding social issues, for example, the artwork of Eko Nugroho; the writing of Pramoedya Ananta Toer and Kartini; the use of Kak in some activist contexts as a gender-neutral alternative to Ibu and Bapak

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing traditional methods that Indonesian speakers use to preserve language and culture; comparing these with examples of cultural artefacts such as dance, songs, artwork, artefacts or traditions, from a range of different cultures; and identifying how they strengthen connections to values and identity, for example, discussing the significance of a possum-skin coat for some Aboriginal Peoples and sharing similarities and differences between cultural artefacts in other languages and cultures represented in the classroom

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10CM01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts to exchange ideas, experiences and opinions about their own and others’ personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using familiar expressions to excuse and apologise, clarify and make requests, for example, Permisi dulu; Minta maaf; Maafkan saya; Maaf, saya terlambat; Boleh minta tolong, Pak; Bagaimana kita …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in conversations, using strategies to sustain interactions (e.g. Saya kurang mengerti; Maaf, tolong diulangi; Bagaimana …?; Sekali lagi?; Apa artinya …?) and using active listening strategies to continue a conversation or phone call, for example, Dengan siapa ini?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a conversation challenge where pairs of students must extend a conversation as long as they can through extension strategies

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing aspects of their own identity and personal worlds with peers, for example, describing significant events, role models and pastimes

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with peers to share experiences of and opinions about teenage life such as responsibilities, relationships and aspirations, for example, Tugas saya mencuci piring setiap malam; Kami cuma makan makanan halal; Pada masa depan, saya mau menjadi penulis di Indonesia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions to clarify or elicit a more detailed response such as after a classmate’s presentation, for example, Maaf, bisa dijelaskan menggunakan contoh tentang …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using culturally appropriate words to request that others do something, for example, minta, harap, mohon, tolong

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing empathy, well-wishing or recognition of success, for example, Kasihan!; Wah, hebat!; Selamat!; Semoga sukses dalam ujian/kompetisi …; Semoga cepat sembuh

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spontaneous interjections and exclamations to show interest, comprehension and fill pauses, for example, Hebaaat!; Asyik!; Oh, begitu!; Apa ya?; Begini …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM01-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating through secure digital spaces such as text messages using informal abbreviations, for example, gk; ku; krn; dgn

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10CM02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use Indonesian language in exchanges to question, offer ideas and opinions, negotiate, compare and discuss

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a class forum, discussing issues and events and responding to questions about their opinions, for example, Pada pendapat saya …; Saya setuju …; Saya kurang pasti …; Pengalaman saya …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in class discussions, expressing opinions (e.g. Mengapa kamu pikir begitu? Saya rasa …; Menurut pendapat saya …; Kalau saya tidak salah …) and making connections with contributions from others, for example, Saya setuju dengan … karena …; Pengalaman saya juga begitu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contrasting the daily life of young people in Indonesia and Australia, and discussing preferences (e.g. Saya suka tidur, jadi saya tidak mau ke sekolah jam 6 pagi; Saya tidak suka naik bis ke sekolah; Saya mau bersepeda motor ke sekolah) and collating results on a comparative table

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging personal views on topics such as education, relationships, sustainability, employment, health and music by participating in a simple debate/class discussion about these issues, for example, Pada pendapat saya …; Dari pihak saya; Saya kurang setuju karena …; Walaupun …; Demikian …

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing print or digital information in Indonesian for real or imagined Indonesian visitors to the school, for example, preparing welcome speeches, filming an introduction to the school or conducting guided tours of the school

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating differences between personal opinions, for example, designing the ideal home (e.g. types of shared spaces, outdoor areas, number of bedrooms/bathrooms); creating a debate on the advantages and disadvantages of participating in team sports

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions and comparisons about school rules and offering suggestions for changes (e.g. tidak adil, tidak diperlukan, dilarang, mungkin lebih baik kalau, bagaimana kalau…?) and brainstorming an issue that relates to the students/school, then writing and practising an oral presentation to the principal suggesting a new idea or change

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions of a guest speaker about Indonesian-speaking community events, for example, Bagaimana perayaan Hari Kemerdekaan Indonesia di kota Bendigo?; Bisakah saya belajar tarian Bali di Victoria?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: debating views on local and global issues such as pollution, mental health and social media, using descriptive and expressive language to persuade the audience, for example, Karena makin lama makin banyak sampah, marilah kita semua bergotong royong untuk …; Penting untuk menjaga keseimbangan antara belajar, bersantai dan bergaul dengan teman

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV1
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews influence local and global action and, therefore, impact the interdependence of Earth’s systems. Worldviews can play a crucial role in achieving sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and completing tasks involving authentic or simulated transactions such as planning a holiday or purchasing goods (e.g. Bagaimana kalau kami ke Danau Toba?; Bisa tawar-menawar?), including culturally appropriate non-verbal gestures to accompany dialogue

elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to decide responsibilities and roles in a class activity, for example, discussing with classmates what to include in a travel brochure, aspects of an Indonesian history presentation or a multimodal presentation on a school issue, for example, Sebaiknya kita mengumpulkan informasi dulu; Bolehkah kita membuat video daripada poster?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in simulated scenarios, for example, enquiring about student exchange programs or interviewing for a scholarship, including culturally appropriate non-verbal gestures to accompany dialogue

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the success of a school activity, excursion or event using a collaborative secure digital format to provide feedback, for example, Saya suka menyanyi lagu …; Saya senang pergi ke galeri karena …; Bagaimana pendapat kamu tentang Museum …?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the comments function on a shared document or posting replies to a post on a secure digital platform to create collaborative texts such as a poster advertising a class party or a storybook to read to a buddy class in a primary school, for example, Apa itu, panjat pinang?; Seharusnya kita minta izin dulu kalau pakai foto dia?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing reflections on their experience of learning Indonesian, discussing progress, challenges and achievements

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10CM04 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpret and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to context, purpose and audience
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching how young people celebrate significant or special events such as birthdays, holidays, celebrations or sporting events in Indonesia and Australia, and sharing findings in a preferred mode of presentation

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing texts on celebrations, environmental issues or health and sharing information in infographics or multimodal texts, for example, Jangan lupa, daur ulang; Awas; Perhatian; Mohon maaf lahir dan batin

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information from audio, written and visual texts and using a preferred method of presentation to share specific ideas about topics such as youth and environmental issues, for example, Masalah-masalah yang dihadapi remaja di kota besar adalah tekanan teman sebaya dan isu lingkungan.

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing short informative texts (e.g. documentary excerpts, news reports), and responding, for example, creating an informative speech about the dangers of climate change or student stress, using appropriate language for the context and audience

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV1
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews influence local and global action and, therefore, impact the interdependence of Earth’s systems. Worldviews can play a crucial role in achieving sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching aspects of Indonesian society, geography, history and culture such as Krakatoa; bencana alam; naik Haji; Hari Raya Idul Fitri; Ogoh-ogoh; nasi tumpeng, or prominent historical figures such as Cut Nyak Dien, Sukarno and other significant cultural influencers, using secure digital tools to present information to specified audiences

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing a variety of texts to identify information (e.g. using websites and tourist brochures to research and match travel destination requirements for a variety of travellers with diverse needs, to align restaurants with diners and sporting interests with games), for example, liburan ekowisata; liburan belanja; liburan mewah; liburan petualangan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing text types and style of writing in Indonesian and English texts, identifying audience and purpose to respond appropriately, for example, listening to the welcome speech by the principal of an Indonesian sister school and responding in a culturally appropriate way such as Assalamalaikum; Walaikum salam

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing and interpreting texts for different purposes and adjusting responses to suit the context and audience, for example, responding to an advertisement about an eco-friendly tourist village and writing a blog post, reading an article about sustainable transport or animal protection and writing a response to the editor

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD1
organising_ideas.text: Responsibly designed products and services aim to minimise the human impact on the environment and restore the quality, ecological integrity and diversity of economic, social, environmental and cultural systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing television programs and films with subtitles, and examining the accuracy and/or the cultural appropriateness of the subtitles (Indonesian/English and English/Indonesian)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10CM05 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking clarification when non-verbal, spoken and written meaning is not understood, by modifying their own language, asking for information to be repeated and finding phrases or expressions with similar meaning, for example, Tolong diulang; Boleh minta penjelasan?; Apakah ini berarti …?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding meaning in context by focusing on known phrases and expressions to interpret new and unknown expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: paying attention to gestures and body language in combination with applying listening strategies to interpret cultural meaning of unfamiliar phrases and expressions when listening to and viewing interactions, for example, watching short video clips

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use bilingual dictionaries and online translation tools, identifying issues such as multiple meanings of words and the need to consider context and understanding of cultural meaning, for example, jam karet

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting signs, text messages or advertisements in Indonesian, identifying language structures and features that are not easily translated and may cause misunderstandings, and writing simple explanations of meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting meaning from key expressions that do not directly translate from English to Indonesian, and finding their Indonesian equivalent based on the intended meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing texts such as commercials, popular music videos and teacher-curated social media posts showing different representations of Indonesian culture, and reflecting on key messages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying strategies to interpret and translate expressions of Australian culture to Indonesian audiences (e.g. ‘go bush’, ‘the outback’, ‘she’ll be right’, ‘schoolies’) and Indonesian culture to Australian audiences (e.g. gotong royong, mudik), and considering how these might be expressed for audiences with different cultural perspectives

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of grammatical rules and context when using dictionaries, to recognise the base word to interpret and translate meaning, for example, mendengarkan – dengar; berbicara – bicara

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM05-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing terms of address and gestures used in different contexts and experimenting with using them, for example, viewing people making speeches in different contexts and adapting the introductions in students’ own presentations; considering who the audience is and how they should be addressed; trying out different greeting gestures such as salim

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10CM06 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts and purposes, to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing presentations about aspects of daily life and practices in Indonesia such as school, leisure, entertainment for specified audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts about topics such as recycling, sustainability, education or city/village life using suitable vocabulary, expressions and textual conventions to match the text type, for example, posters, infographics

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting a report on an issue, recent event or public figure, using graphics to support meaning, for example, Olimpiade, bencana alam, hari Bumi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding with Indonesian-speaking peers in Indonesia and Australia through email, shared secure digital spaces or video, comparing topics of interest, language choices and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing own texts such as scripts for film or television, comics or short stories, with imaginary people, places or experiences, for example, setting a story in the past or future; creating a new species; imagining space travel; inventing a superhero, detective or an alter ego

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating, performing and recording a range of texts (e.g. songs, raps and skits) to entertain others, including experimenting with Indonesian artforms such as a wayang performance, dongeng or sinetron

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or reading Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ stories in English, and adapting them to share with an Indonesian-speaking audience, considering words and concepts that are not easily translated and ways to use visuals to aid understanding

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying ongoing collaboration of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists and artists from Indonesia, for example, learning about batik making in central Australia, rock art in northern Australia and similar art forms in Indonesia, and developing a video or slideshow showing similarities and differences between these art forms

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASG2
organising_ideas.text: Australia and Asia are interdependent through a range of historical and contemporary connections.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a new aspect of a text such as a new character, plot, object or perspective, or an alternative ending

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10CM06-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining to others a procedure or practice such as a recipe, the rules of a sport or board game, instructions on keeping a pet/animal, or fashion tips, for example, Tambahkan dua sendok makan susu kental manis; Bersihkan kandang hamster setiap hari

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL01 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken Indonesian to enhance and extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying authentic pitch, rhythm, stress, pronunciation and intonation modelled on Indonesian speech in spoken texts, for example, listening to and imitating Indonesian speakers in radio programs or interviews

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and reproducing sounds such as the glottal stop k and unexploded t at the end of words, and sound combinations such as kh, sy and meny- in words, and ng- at the beginning of words, for example, by doing tongue twisters or reading poetry or song lyrics

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: stressing the correct syllable in polysyllabic words, for example, mendengarkan, membersihkan, and in compound words, for example, dimejahijaukan; bertanggung jawab; menganaktirikan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and reproducing the rhythm of extended sentences such as the correct pausing for clauses in a complex sentence (e.g. Dulu (pause), waktu kecil (pause), saya mau menjadi pilot tetapi sekarang (pause), saya mau menjadi guru), for example, by listening to a short audio clip and reproducing with some vocabulary changes that classmates must identify

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: acquiring an approximation of the trilled r sound in Indonesian, by listening to songs such as Laskar Pelangi

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising complex sounds for fluency using tongue twisters, for example, Kuku kaki kakak-kakakku kaku-kaku kuku kaki kakek-kakekku kaku-kaku

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL01-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronouns or titles to identify people or characters, for example, Mbak, Kak, Kepala Sekolah, Si, Sang, Beliau, by participating in role-plays, re-telling folktales or sharing new stories

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL02 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adjectives of character to describe the qualities of people by playing a Who is it? game, for example, murah hati, besar kepala

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating tense and time using specific time markers, for example, sekali-sekali, belum pernah, tidak pernah, tadi malam, nanti sore, pada masa depan, dua tahun yang lalu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating possibility (e.g. mungkin; mudah-mudahan; semoga; saya harap) when writing ‘a letter to my 21-year-old self’

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: specifying what is being referred to using yang and … nya, for example, yang ini, yang itu, Yang mana? in a shopping role-play; Cuacanya panas sekali hari ini in a diary entry

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using yang in embedded clauses, for example, viewing images and creating captions that contain embedded clauses such as Binatang yang terancam punah termasuk koala dan harimau Sumatra

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating equivalence using adalah, for example, Buku itu adalah buku latihan bahasa Indonesia kelas kami

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Indonesian has base words and that word families are created using affixation (e.g. belajar; mengajar; pelajaran; pengajaran; pengajar; pelajar) by playing digital or online matching games with word pairs

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: adding affixation ke … an to base words to create abstract nouns (e.g. kesehatan; kegiatan; kehidupan) or to indicate that someone or something is affected by the base word, for example, kehujanan; kepanasan; kelaparan

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating action using transitive verbs, me- verbs and understanding the function of suffixes, for example, me … kan; me … I; Jono menaiki gunung; Jono menaikkan bendera; Saya membeli makanan di pasar; Saya membelikan ibu makanan di pasar

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E10 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using di- forms to emphasise the object, for example, Buku dibaca oleh in contrast to Dia membaca buku; Komputernya diambil dari kantor sekolah in contrast to Dia mengambil komputernya dari kantor

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E11 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the person doing an action using pe- prefix, for example, penjual, penari, pelukis

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E12 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the preposition kepada for written exchanges with people and giving things to people, for example, Dia memberi uang kepada adiknya; Saya bertanya kepada guru saya tentang masalah itu

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E13 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using comparatives such as the prefix se- (e.g. sebesar; Dia setinggi adiknya) or lebih … daripada … (e.g. lebih murah … dari pada …) and superlatives ter …, yang paling … (e.g. Stadion itu adalah stadion yang terbesar di seluruh dunia; Dia penyanyi yang paling populer di dunia)

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E14 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: seeking information using interrogatives and question forms playing 20 questions or a Who is it? game, for example, mengapa/kenapa, bagaimana, yang mana, untuk apa/siapa, dengan apa/siapa, berapa, dari mana

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL02-E15 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjunctions to create complex sentences (e.g. supaya/sehingga; namun demikian; walaupun; meskipun; sementara/sambil/sedangkan), for example, in a class debate or writing an evaluative or persuasive article for a school magazine

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL03 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate Indonesian texts, using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how texts are constructed, including cohesive devices such as conjunctions, and coherence devices such as time markers (e.g. Mula-Mula …, Kedua …, Akhirnya …, Di satu pihak …, Di pihak lain …) and comparing with English and/or other languages, creating a comparative table for their personal glossary

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining language structures and features used in a range of texts for communicative effect (e.g. to inform, entertain or persuade), reading short passages and highlighting examples of the target structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on literary devices to enhance ideas such as metaphors in texts (e.g. adalah and simile), for example, sama dengan; seperti; setinggi; bagai

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the prevalence of acronyms known as singkatan (e.g. met ultah, PenJas, narkoba, Jatim), and comparing them with English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in register of language used in texts, and noticing variations such as colloquial language and how it differs from standard forms, creating a chart showing the different forms and adding it to their personal glossary, for example, Kasih aku coklat, dong!; Boleh minta coklat, Bu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying loan words in spoken Indonesian, for example, ngopi; dirilis; meng-upload

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing sentence structures in Indonesian, English and/or other languages they know, and recognising the use of different structures and features used to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and discussing how the linguistic diversity of Indonesia reveals cultural diversity, and recognising how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL03-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting that Indonesian speakers may use gender-neutral language such as pacar, dia and -nya, and that these cannot be translated with equivalence without contextual cues

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIN10UL04 - Indonesian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E01 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: being aware that there are regional and social differences regarding norms of interaction across Indonesia and reflecting that geographical and social differences also influence norms of interaction in Australia and other countries

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK2
organising_ideas.text: The interrelationships between people and the diverse environments and systems across the Asia region have global implications.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E02 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that many expressions and behaviours, such as meeting a friend at a suitable time, are closely related to cultural and religious practices and beliefs (e.g. Saya sholat dulu; Ada upacara potong gigi di pura; Ada kebaktian di gereja; Mau beli jamu dulu), and reading texts or viewing short video clips that outline these cultural practices and discussing within the class

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E03 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Indonesia has a diversity of languages (using a map to create a visual representation of language use), people may be multilingual and that languages are always evolving and changing, for example, bahasa Jawa; bahasa Gaul; bahasa Binan

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E04 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing personal journal entries and participating in group discussions to reflect on and evaluate how learning Indonesian has had an impact on their own assumptions about Indonesian language, culture and identity

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E05 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring intercultural communication, considering how their own cultural ways of thinking and behaving affect attitudes and influence other people’s responses or interpretations and how they change over time

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E06 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and explaining the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place, to present in Indonesian to a group of Indonesian-speaking visitors at a school assembly

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E07 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the influence of language (e.g. noticing how language is used in art, graffiti, online mediums and political protests), and reflecting on how messaging used in public spaces about Reformasi; Keluarga Berencana; Satu nusa, satu bangsa, satu Bahasa, can have an impact on national behaviours and identity

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E08 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the influence of activists, artists and authors on language, art and ways of thinking and how they may influence attitudes and values regarding social issues, for example, the artwork of Eko Nugroho; the writing of Pramoedya Ananta Toer and Kartini; the use of Kak in some activist contexts as a gender-neutral alternative to Ibu and Bapak

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LIN10UL04-E09 - Indonesian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing traditional methods that Indonesian speakers use to preserve language and culture; comparing these with examples of cultural artefacts such as dance, songs, artwork, artefacts or traditions, from a range of different cultures; and identifying how they strengthen connections to values and identity, for example, discussing the significance of a possum-skin coat for some Aboriginal Peoples and sharing similarities and differences between cultural artefacts in other languages and cultures represented in the classroom

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures
